objectives.subject: Use of English
objectives.prompt: What is the central recommendation of the library committee’s report?
options: End every reading competition.
Use evidence about pupils’ needs to guide decisions on library access.

objectives.explanation: The final paragraph prioritises evidence of actual use when deciding how to improve access. Decoration is welcomed but is not the central recommendation.
objectives.passage:
At the beginning of the term, the library committee assumed that pupils borrowed few books because the shelves were unattractive. It spent part of its small grant on paint and labels. Borrowing scarcely changed. Before spending the remaining money, the committee asked pupils to keep a record of unsuccessful visits for one week. Most recorded visits occurred after afternoon clubs, when the library was already closed. Some pupils also said they avoided unfamiliar books because the catalogue listed only titles and authors.

The committee then tried two inexpensive changes. On Tuesdays and Thursdays, a volunteer kept the library open for an additional hour. Pupils also wrote brief recommendations on cards beside books they had enjoyed. Borrowing increased during the following month. However, the committee refused to describe either change as the sole cause. A new reading competition had begun at the same time, and examination preparation might also have influenced pupils’ choices.

For the next term, the committee proposed recording visits, borrowing and opening hours separately. Its report concluded that attractive shelves were welcome, but decisions about access should begin with evidence of how pupils actually used the library. The report did not recommend abandoning decoration altogether.

objectives.subject: Use of English
objectives.prompt: Why did the pupils’ visit records challenge the committee’s original assumption?
options: They identified a practical barrier that repainting could not remove.
They proved that no pupil liked reading.
They showed that every book was unsuitable.
They established that labels always reduce borrowing.
objectives.explanation: Many unsuccessful visits happened after closing time. Attractive shelves cannot help a pupil enter a closed library.

objectives.prompt: What explains the small traders’ concern about crate deposits?
options: A refundable payment can still reduce the cash available for immediate stock purchases.

objectives.explanation: Refundability does not eliminate a short-term cash constraint between payment and refund.
objectives.passage:
When a neighbourhood market introduced reusable delivery crates, some traders welcomed the plan and others objected to the deposit. The market association explained that the deposit would be returned when an undamaged crate came back. Nevertheless, several small traders worried that money tied up in deposits would leave them unable to buy enough stock for the following morning.

For the first six weeks, the association allowed traders to share crates and returned deposits on the same day. It also weighed discarded packaging at the end of each market day. The recorded weight fell, although the records did not include packaging taken home by customers. The association therefore described the result as a reduction in waste collected at the market, rather than proof that all waste from market purchases had fallen.

A trader who had initially objected later supported the scheme, saying that fewer broken containers had reduced losses during transport. Another trader remained unconvinced because her supplier would not accept the crates. The association decided to meet suppliers before expanding the scheme. Its chairperson argued that a useful environmental policy should consider how goods move through the entire supply chain, including the businesses that are least able to absorb additional costs.

objectives.subject: Use of English
objectives.prompt: Why does the market report distinguish collected waste from all waste arising from purchases?
options: No packaging was ever used at the market.
Customers were required to leave every container behind.
The association had measured every customer’s household waste.
Its measurements covered only waste left at the market.
objectives.explanation: Packaging taken home was outside the records, so a claim about total waste would exceed the measured evidence.

objectives.subject: Use of English
objectives.prompt: Which action most directly addresses the objection of the trader whose supplier would not accept crates?
options: Increase the deposit without consultation.
Stop recording discarded packaging.
Discuss compatible packaging arrangements with suppliers.
Repaint the market sign.
objectives.explanation: Her stated barrier concerns supplier acceptance, so cooperation along the supply chain addresses it more directly than publicity alone.

objectives.subject: Use of English
objectives.prompt: What does “absorb additional costs” mean in the market passage?
options: Prove that suppliers never charge fees.
Bear extra expenses without passing them on or being unable to operate.
Collect damaged containers from the road.
Measure the weight of unsold stock.
objectives.explanation: Absorb is used financially: a business carries a cost rather than treating it as a physical substance.

objectives.subject: Use of English
objectives.prompt: Which description best captures the chairperson’s position on the crate scheme?
options: Support environmental improvement while examining its practical effects on different businesses.
Reject environmental policies in every situation.
Ignore smaller traders to maximise deposits.
Expand immediately without meeting suppliers.
objectives.explanation: The chairperson supports a useful environmental policy but requires attention to supply chains and vulnerable businesses.

objectives.subject: English Language
objectives.prompt: Choose the correct completion: The quality of the laboratory reports ___ improved.
options: have
are
were
has
objectives.explanation: The head of the subject is the singular noun quality; reports is inside a modifying phrase.

objectives.subject: English Language
objectives.prompt: Which sentence punctuates a non-restrictive clause correctly?
options: Mrs Bello, who coaches the choir addressed the pupils.
Mrs Bello who coaches the choir, addressed, the pupils.
Mrs Bello, who coaches the choir, addressed the pupils.
Mrs Bello who coaches, the choir addressed the pupils.
objectives.explanation: The extra information about the named person is set off with a pair of commas.

objectives.subject: English Language
objectives.prompt: Complete the sentence: This instrument is superior ___ the one we used last year.
options: over
to
than
from
objectives.explanation: The adjective superior takes to in this comparison, rather than than.

objectives.subject: English Language
objectives.prompt: Choose the sentence with correct parallel structure.
options: The course teaches learners to measure, to record and to compare.
The course teaches learners to measure, recording and comparison.
The course teaches learners measurement, to record and comparing.
The course teaches learners to measuring, to record and comparison.
objectives.explanation: All three coordinated actions use matching infinitive forms.

objectives.subject: English Language
objectives.prompt: Which version makes it clear that Halima, rather than her sister, won the prize?
options: Halima thanked her sister because she won the prize.
She thanked her sister when she won the prize.
Halima told her sister that she had won the prize.
Halima, who won the prize, thanked her sister.
objectives.explanation: The relative clause directly modifies Halima, so the winner is unambiguous.

objectives.subject: English Language
objectives.prompt: Choose the correctly formed passive version of “The panel will announce the result tomorrow.”
options: The result has announce by the panel tomorrow.
The result was announce by the panel tomorrow.
The result will be announced by the panel tomorrow.
The result will announced by the panel tomorrow.
objectives.explanation: The object becomes the subject and the passive retains will + be + past participle.

objectives.subject: English Language
objectives.prompt: The manager called the explanation plausible but asked for evidence. Plausible means
options: deliberately insulting
apparently reasonable
certainly false
fully proved
objectives.explanation: A plausible explanation seems reasonable, but the request for evidence shows it is not yet established as true.

objectives.subject: English Language
objectives.prompt: What does “read between the lines” mean in “To understand the letter, you must read between the lines”?
options: Infer meanings that are suggested rather than directly stated.
Read only alternate lines aloud.
Ignore the writer’s tone completely.
Copy the letter without punctuation.
objectives.explanation: The idiom concerns implicit meaning, not the physical spaces on a page.

objectives.subject: English Language
objectives.prompt: Choose the word opposite in meaning to impartial in “We need an impartial judge.”
options: patient
experienced
careful
biased
objectives.explanation: Impartial means fair and not favouring a side; biased expresses the opposite.

objectives.subject: English Language
objectives.prompt: In “The speaker digressed before returning to the budget,” digressed means
options: ended the meeting permanently
proved the budget was balanced
moved away from the main topic
repeated the final calculation
objectives.explanation: Returning to the budget signals that the speaker had temporarily left the subject.

objectives.subject: English Language
objectives.prompt: Choose the expression most appropriate in a bank: The customer requested a printed ___ of transactions on the account.
options: syllabus
statement
diagnosis
verdict
objectives.explanation: An account statement records transactions over a period.

objectives.subject: English Language
objectives.prompt: Which linking expression introduces a specific illustration? “Several local materials can be reused. ___, clean jars can store seeds.”
options: For instance
In contrast
Consequently
Despite this
objectives.explanation: The second sentence supplies an example of the general statement.

objectives.subject: English Language
objectives.prompt: Which sentence is most appropriate in a formal laboratory report?
options: The stuff went funny and looked somehow.
Honestly, that liquid was just amazing!
You know, we did a thing with heat.
The solution changed from blue to colourless after heating.
objectives.explanation: It reports an observable result precisely and avoids slang or personal judgement.

objectives.subject: English Language
objectives.prompt: Choose the correct completion: There is ___ sugar in this cup than in that one.
options: fewest
many
less
fewer
objectives.explanation: Sugar is an uncountable mass noun here, so the comparison uses less.

objectives.subject: English Language
objectives.prompt: Which sentence places only so that it means the teacher marked the essays and no other work?
options: The teacher marked the essays only yesterday.
The teacher marked only the essays.
Only the teacher marked the essays.
The teacher only marked the essays.
objectives.explanation: Only immediately limits the object the essays. Placing it elsewhere changes what is restricted.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: An apprentice can spend Saturday earning ₦8,000 at a paid job or attending a free training session. She attends the training and gives up no other benefit. What is the opportunity cost of attending?
options: The training organiser’s total expenses.
Every job she might ever obtain.
The ₦8,000 earnings forgone.
Zero because training is free.
objectives.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the next-best alternative sacrificed, even when the chosen activity has no monetary fee.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: A point inside a production possibility frontier represents an economy that
options: cannot produce either good at all.
could increase at least one output without reducing the other, using available resources more efficiently.
must already use all resources efficiently.
has an unattainable combination of outputs.
objectives.explanation: Interior points imply unemployment or inefficiency relative to the attainable frontier.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: Which arrangement best illustrates a mixed economy?
options: Private firms operate alongside public enterprises and regulation.
All productive assets belong to the state.
Every economic decision is made by household custom.
Government is prohibited from owning any enterprise.
objectives.explanation: A mixed economy combines market allocation and a government role rather than relying exclusively on either.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: A market survey reports a mean income of ₦90,000 but a median of ₦35,000. Which explanation is consistent with these figures?
options: Every respondent earned exactly ₦90,000.
More than half must earn exactly ₦90,000.
The median must always exceed the mean.
A few very high incomes may have raised the mean.
objectives.explanation: The mean is sensitive to extreme values, while the median depends on the middle position. The figures alone do not prove the exact distribution.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: A household spends ₦18,000 of its ₦60,000 monthly budget on transport. What angle represents transport in a pie chart?
objectives.explanation: Transport is 18,000/60,000 = 0.3 of spending. Multiply by 360° to obtain 108°.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: The price of a substitute for locally made soap rises while all other determinants remain unchanged. What is the likely initial effect on demand for the local soap?
options: Its demand curve must shift left.
Its demand curve shifts to the right.
Its own supply curve must shift left.
There is only movement down its unchanged demand curve.
objectives.explanation: Buyers may switch from the now dearer substitute, increasing local soap demand at each own price.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: Improved seed technology lowers rice production costs while demand is unchanged. In a competitive market, which result is most likely?
options: A lower equilibrium price and a larger equilibrium quantity.
A higher price and a smaller quantity.
A lower price and a smaller quantity.
A higher price and an unchanged quantity.
objectives.explanation: Lower costs increase supply, shifting its curve right. With downward-sloping demand, equilibrium price falls and quantity rises.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: A product has price elasticity of demand of magnitude 0.4 over the relevant range. What is the likely effect of a small price rise on total sales revenue, other things equal?
options: Revenue necessarily falls by 40%.
Quantity demanded rises faster than price.
Revenue is always unchanged when demand is inelastic.
Revenue rises because quantity falls proportionately less than price rises.
objectives.explanation: Demand is inelastic: the percentage loss in quantity is smaller than the percentage gain in price for a small change.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: Using initial values as the percentage-change base, price rises from ₦200 to ₦220 and quantity demanded falls from 500 to 450. What is the magnitude of price elasticity of demand?
objectives.explanation: Quantity falls by 50/500 = 10%; price rises by 20/200 = 10%. The ratio of magnitudes is 1.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: When more workers are added to a fixed workshop, output eventually rises by smaller amounts. Which principle does this illustrate?
options: Perfectly elastic supply of every factor.
Diminishing marginal returns.
Increasing returns to scale under proportional expansion.
A permanent fall in total output from the first worker.
objectives.explanation: With a fixed factor and unchanged technology, additional variable inputs can eventually add less to output.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: A firm’s total cost rises from ₦42,000 to ₦46,000 when output rises from 100 to 110 units. What is marginal cost per additional unit over this interval?
objectives.explanation: Marginal cost over the interval is change in total cost divided by change in output: ₦4,000/10 = ₦400.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: Which cost must a firm pay in the short run even when its output is zero?
options: Packaging used only for sold units.
Piece-rate wages paid only for each unit produced.
Raw materials consumed only when production occurs.
Rent on a factory under an existing fixed lease.
objectives.explanation: A contractual lease payment does not vary with current output over the short-run period.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: A competitive firm faces a market price it cannot influence. Its demand curve for its own output is conventionally drawn as
options: the same as the downward-sloping industry demand curve.
upward sloping because it controls the market.
horizontal at the market price.
vertical at the industry’s total output.
objectives.explanation: A price-taking firm can sell at the given market price; raising its price would lose buyers to competitors in the model.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: Which barrier can help a monopoly persist?
options: An unlimited number of equally efficient existing suppliers.
Exclusive legal control of a necessary patented process.
Perfect freedom of entry for identical rivals.
Complete absence of product differentiation and barriers.
objectives.explanation: A legally protected process can restrict entry and prevent rivals from offering equivalent output using that process.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: When inflation reduces the amount of goods a fixed cash balance can buy, which function of money is most directly weakened?
options: Store of value.
Unit of physical weight.
Source of unlimited real resources.
Guarantee of constant relative prices.
objectives.explanation: Money held over time loses purchasing power, making it a less reliable store of real value.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: A central bank raises its policy interest rate to restrain inflation. Through the borrowing-cost channel, what is the intended effect?
options: All prices fall instantly by the policy-rate increase.
Every bank must stop accepting deposits.
Government revenue automatically becomes zero.
Higher borrowing costs reduce some consumption and investment spending.
objectives.explanation: More expensive credit can reduce interest-sensitive spending and aggregate demand; the effect is not immediate or guaranteed.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: Which transaction belongs to current domestic production in a year’s GDP?
options: The resale value of a used bicycle produced five years ago.
A pension transfer with no current service provided.
Payment for a newly provided tailoring service.
A cash gift from a parent to a child.
objectives.explanation: GDP counts the value of current final production. Transfers and resale of old assets do not themselves represent new output.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: Nominal output rises while the general price level rises by the same proportion. What follows about real output, using the matching price index?
options: Real output must become negative.
Real output is unchanged.
Real output must double.
The nominal figure alone proves living standards improved.
objectives.explanation: Real output removes the price-level effect; equal proportional increases in nominal output and the deflator cancel.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: A tax takes a smaller percentage of income as a household’s income rises. The tax is
options: regressive.
progressive.
proportional.
a subsidy.
objectives.explanation: Regressivity concerns the share of income paid, not whether the richer household pays more naira in total.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: Which spending is capital expenditure in a government budget?
options: Monthly salaries for existing clerks.
Payment for this month’s office electricity.
Purchase of stationery consumed this week.
Construction of a new public bridge.
objectives.explanation: Capital expenditure creates a durable asset, unlike routine wages, utility bills or recurring supplies.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: Country A sacrifices 2 bags of rice to produce one bale of cloth; country B sacrifices 5 bags for the same bale. Who has comparative advantage in cloth?
options: Neither country, because cloth is measured in bales.
Both countries must have identical opportunity costs.
Country A, because its opportunity cost of cloth is lower.
Country B, because it sacrifices more rice.
objectives.explanation: Comparative advantage depends on opportunity cost: 2 bags of rice is less than 5.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: The naira depreciates against a supplier’s currency while the foreign-currency price of imported machinery stays fixed. What happens to its naira price before other charges?
options: It becomes independent of the exchange rate.
It rises.
It falls to zero.
It is necessarily unchanged.
objectives.explanation: Depreciation means more naira are needed to buy the same amount of the supplier’s currency.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: Why may rapid GDP growth fail to reduce poverty substantially?
options: Growth benefits may be concentrated among a small share of the population.
GDP growth requires every household’s income to rise equally.
Poverty depends only on the number of banknotes printed.
Unequal distribution is impossible during growth.
objectives.explanation: An increase in total output does not by itself specify distribution, employment access or household poverty outcomes.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: A qualified worker stops searching for work because repeated applications have failed. Why might an unemployment rate understate labour-market distress?
options: Every employed worker is classified as unemployed.
Leaving the labour force always creates a new job.
The measure necessarily counts all children as unemployed.
Discouraged people outside the measured labour force may be excluded.
objectives.explanation: Many unemployment measures require active job search, so discouraged non-searchers may not be counted as unemployed.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: Which policy most directly raises labour productivity through human capital?
options: Printing currency without changing skills or equipment.
Reducing maintenance of productive equipment.
Relevant training that improves workers’ skills.
Renaming an existing ministry.
objectives.explanation: Human capital is productive knowledge and skill embodied in people; effective training can increase output per worker.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: Which statement is normative rather than positive?
options: The budget allocated ₦20 million to clinics.
Government ought to place a higher priority on rural clinics.
The town has three clinics.
Clinic attendance rose last month.
objectives.explanation: Ought to expresses a value judgement. The other statements describe claims that can be checked against evidence.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: A production possibility frontier shifts outward after widespread improvements in productive technology. What does this show?
options: The economy’s production capacity has increased.
Only the composition of demand has changed.
Every resource has become unemployed.
The economy must produce beyond all feasible limits.
objectives.explanation: An outward shift expands attainable output combinations; a movement along an unchanged frontier only reallocates existing capacity.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: Why can a bar chart drawn with an unlabelled, truncated vertical axis mislead readers?
options: It necessarily changes the underlying observations.
It proves that every number is false.
It prevents readers from identifying any categories.
It can exaggerate the apparent size of differences.
objectives.explanation: Starting the axis above zero without clear labelling may make small absolute differences appear visually large.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: If consumers’ income rises and demand for a particular cheap staple falls, that staple is classified, over this income range, as
options: a public good solely because it is cheap.
a good with zero demand at every price.
an inferior good.
a normal good.
objectives.explanation: An inferior good has negative income elasticity: demand decreases as income increases, other factors equal.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: A binding maximum price is set below the competitive equilibrium price. What is the immediate market imbalance, other things equal?
options: Demand must become zero.
Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.
Quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded.
Supply becomes unlimited.
objectives.explanation: At the lower controlled price, consumers wish to buy more while suppliers offer less, creating a shortage.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: Which situation tends to make demand more price elastic?
options: Consumers have several close substitutes and time to adjust.
The good has no substitutes and is urgently needed.
Consumers cannot change any purchase during the period.
The good is the only available life-saving treatment.
objectives.explanation: Substitutes and adjustment time make it easier to reduce purchases when price rises.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: Which example is an external economy of scale for a group of firms?
options: One firm buys its own larger machine.
A single manager negotiates a discount on that firm’s order.
One firm reorganises its own accounting department.
A growing industrial area attracts specialist suppliers that lower local firms’ input costs.
objectives.explanation: The benefit arises from the industry’s or cluster’s expansion, rather than the expansion of one firm alone.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: Product differentiation is particularly associated with which market model?
options: A pure monopoly with no rival producer.
A market in which no goods are sold.
Monopolistic competition.
Perfect competition with identical products.
objectives.explanation: Many firms sell products perceived as different while entry is relatively open; differentiation gives each some pricing discretion.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: Which institution normally has primary responsibility for issuing a country’s legal-tender banknotes?
options: A private insurance broker.
The central bank or designated monetary authority.
Every licensed supermarket.
A cooperative thrift society.
objectives.explanation: Currency issuance is a monetary-authority function; ordinary retail firms and insurers do not issue national legal tender.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: Why is barter difficult when a farmer wants shoes but the shoemaker does not want farm produce?
options: There is no double coincidence of wants.
Both parties already use the same currency.
The farmer’s produce is automatically worthless.
Every barter transaction requires a bank loan.
objectives.explanation: Direct exchange requires each party to want what the other offers at the same time.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: Which adjustment converts gross domestic product to net domestic product?
options: Add the value of all intermediate goods again.
Subtract all household consumption.
Multiply output by the unemployment rate.
Subtract depreciation of fixed capital.
objectives.explanation: Depreciation accounts for capital consumed or worn out during production; gross minus depreciation gives net.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: A government spends more than its revenue in a financial year. The difference is a
options: trade surplus.
balanced budget.
budget deficit.
budget surplus.
objectives.explanation: A deficit is the excess of expenditure over revenue for the period; debt is the accumulated stock of outstanding borrowing.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: Which item is normally recorded as an export of services?
options: A resident buys locally produced bread from a nearby bakery.
A resident consulting firm earns fees from a client abroad.
A shop imports phones for local sale.
Two local households exchange used furniture.
objectives.explanation: The resident supplies a service to a non-resident. A merchandise import and a domestic transaction are different categories.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: A worker’s nominal wage rises by 5% while consumer prices rise by 12%. What happens to the purchasing power of the wage?
options: It falls.
It rises by 17%.
It is guaranteed to remain unchanged.
It rises because any nominal increase is a real increase.
objectives.explanation: The wage grows more slowly than prices, so it buys fewer goods and services. The exact real change is 1.05/1.12 minus 1.

objectives.subject: Economics
objectives.prompt: Which situation most clearly illustrates underemployment?
options: A nurse voluntarily works reduced hours and wants no more work.
A full-time teacher works the hours she wants.
A retired person does not want employment.
A trained electrician wants full-time electrical work but can obtain only a few hours of it each week.
objectives.explanation: Insufficient available hours relative to desired work indicate time-related underemployment. The other examples do not show inadequate work hours.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: A cell has a cellulose wall, chloroplasts and a large permanent vacuole. Which identification is best supported?
options: A mature mammalian red blood cell.
A bacterial cell with a membrane-bound nucleus.
An animal muscle cell.
A photosynthetic plant cell.
objectives.explanation: The combination of a cellulose wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole is characteristic of a photosynthetic plant cell.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: A plant cell is placed in a solution with lower water potential than its cell sap. What is the initial net movement of water?
options: Equally out of both the cell wall and nucleus only.
No movement because a cell wall makes water movement impossible.
Out of the cell through its partially permeable membrane.
Into the cell against the water-potential gradient without energy.
objectives.explanation: Water moves by osmosis from higher to lower water potential across a partially permeable membrane.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: Which observation most directly indicates active transport of mineral ions into root cells?
options: Particles spread through still air without metabolic energy.
Uptake continues against the concentration gradient and decreases when respiration is inhibited.
Ions move from higher to lower concentration in water without cells.
Water crosses a membrane towards lower water potential.
objectives.explanation: Movement against a gradient requires energy; sensitivity to inhibited respiration supports energy-dependent transport.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: A destarched variegated leaf is exposed to light and tested for starch. Only the previously green regions turn blue-black. What does this result support?
options: Chlorophyll-containing regions produced starch under the experimental conditions.
White regions contain more starch than green regions.
All plant tissue photosynthesises without pigments.
Iodine turns every living cell blue-black.
objectives.explanation: The colour change localises starch to green tissue. It supports a role for chlorophyll but does not prove that light or carbon dioxide is unnecessary.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: What is the main digestive role of bile in the small intestine?
options: It is a protease that digests proteins.
It converts starch directly to amino acids.
It transports oxygen to intestinal cells.
It emulsifies fats, increasing surface area available to lipase.
objectives.explanation: Bile salts break large fat droplets into smaller droplets. Bile is not itself the enzyme that hydrolyses fat.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: A food sample gives a violet colour in the biuret test. Which nutrient class is indicated?
options: Reducing sugar.
Pure water.
Protein.
Starch.
objectives.explanation: The biuret reaction detects peptide bonds and gives a violet colour with proteins under suitable conditions.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: Why does the left ventricle have a thicker muscular wall than the right ventricle?
options: Its wall must filter urea from blood.
It must generate pressure to drive blood through the systemic circulation.
It contains only deoxygenated blood.
It pumps blood only to the nearby lungs.
objectives.explanation: The left ventricle pumps around the body against greater overall resistance than the pulmonary circuit.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: Which feature of mammalian alveoli most directly reduces the diffusion distance for gases?
options: A very thin exchange surface.
Thick layers of keratin.
A complete absence of capillaries.
A dry impermeable surface.
objectives.explanation: Thin alveolar and capillary walls create a short path for oxygen and carbon dioxide diffusion.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: Ring-barking removes a complete strip of bark including phloem but leaves xylem intact. Why may swelling occur above the ring?
options: Xylem immediately changes into starch.
All upward water movement must stop at once.
Roots begin photosynthesising inside the bark.
Sugars transported in phloem accumulate above the interruption.
objectives.explanation: Removing phloem disrupts translocation from leaves to lower sinks, so assimilates may accumulate above the damaged region.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: When body temperature rises, which response helps increase heat loss?
options: Increased involuntary shivering.
Reduced sweat secretion as the only cooling mechanism.
Dilation of blood vessels supplying the skin.
Constriction of skin blood vessels in every case.
objectives.explanation: Vasodilation increases blood flow near the skin surface, supporting transfer of heat to cooler surroundings.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: In a reflex arc, what is the role of the sensory neurone?
options: Carry impulses from the spinal cord to a muscle only.
Carry impulses from a receptor towards the central nervous system.
Carry hormones from a gland through blood.
Contract directly as the muscle effector.
objectives.explanation: A sensory neurone links detection at a receptor to processing in the central nervous system.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: What is pollination in a flowering plant?
options: Transfer of pollen from an anther to a stigma.
Fusion of a sperm nucleus with an egg nucleus.
Development of an ovary into a fruit.
Dispersal of a mature seed away from the parent.
objectives.explanation: Pollination is pollen transfer. Fusion of gametes occurs later during fertilisation.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: Why does meiosis normally precede sexual reproduction in a diploid life cycle?
options: It doubles the chromosome number in every gamete.
It guarantees that every offspring is genetically identical.
It replaces fertilisation with binary fission.
It produces haploid cells so fertilisation can restore the diploid number.
objectives.explanation: Reduction division halves chromosome number, preventing doubling at each generation when gametes fuse.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: In a monohybrid cross Tt × Tt with complete dominance, what fraction of offspring is expected to be homozygous recessive?
objectives.explanation: The four equally likely genotype combinations are TT, Tt, Tt and tt; one is homozygous recessive.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: A plant with a dominant phenotype is crossed with a homozygous recessive plant. A large offspring sample contains both phenotypes. Under a single-gene complete-dominance model, what does this show?
options: The dominant allele has disappeared from all offspring.
The dominant-phenotype parent is heterozygous.
The recessive parent must be homozygous dominant.
Every offspring must be a new species.
objectives.explanation: A recessive offspring must receive a recessive allele from each parent; the parent showing dominance therefore carries both alleles.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: A student samples grass cover only beside a football pitch and generalises to the whole school compound. What is the main weakness?
options: The selected location may not represent the full range of habitats.
Quadrats can never be used for plants.
Grass cover cannot vary between locations.
Sampling more areas would always make the result less reliable.
objectives.explanation: A convenience location can bias an estimate when conditions differ elsewhere; more quadrats at the same biased location do not necessarily fix representativeness.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: In the chain grass → grasshopper → lizard → hawk, which organism is the secondary consumer?
options: Grass.
Grasshopper.
Hawk.
Lizard.
objectives.explanation: The grasshopper is the primary consumer feeding on the producer; the lizard eats that primary consumer.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: Why can excessive fertiliser runoff lead to low dissolved oxygen in a pond?
options: Every algal cell permanently stops respiration.
Water can contain oxygen only when no organisms are present.
Increased algal biomass can later fuel decomposition that consumes oxygen.
Fertiliser turns all oxygen directly into nitrogen gas.
objectives.explanation: Nutrient enrichment promotes growth; respiration by decomposers breaking down dead biomass can reduce dissolved oxygen.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: Which feature distinguishes insects from spiders among adult arthropods?
options: Only insects possess an exoskeleton.
Insects normally have three pairs of walking legs.
All insects have eight walking legs.
Only insects have jointed appendages.
objectives.explanation: Adult insects have six legs; spiders have four pairs. Both groups have jointed appendages, so that feature alone does not distinguish them.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: During a drought, plants with an inherited ability to reduce water loss leave more offspring. Which statement best describes natural selection in this case?
options: The inherited water-saving trait becomes more frequent through differential reproductive success.
Every plant consciously changes its genes.
Drought creates identical useful mutations in all plants.
Survival differences cannot affect future generations.
objectives.explanation: Selection acts on existing heritable variation; it does not require every individual to acquire a trait because it needs it.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: Which organelle is the principal site of aerobic ATP production in a typical plant root cell?
options: Chloroplast.
Cell wall.
Large vacuole.
Mitochondrion.
objectives.explanation: Root cells respire; mitochondria carry out key stages of aerobic respiration even in cells that do not photosynthesise.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: A freshly cut potato strip becomes firm after standing in distilled water. Which explanation is best?
options: Water moves out of every cell into distilled water.
The cell walls dissolve and form bone.
Water enters cells by osmosis and increases turgor.
Starch is instantly converted into a new cell wall.
objectives.explanation: Water entry expands the vacuole and presses the contents against the wall, increasing tissue firmness.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: Why is a leaf first boiled in water during a starch test?
options: To make iodine unnecessary.
To kill the tissue and stop its metabolic reactions.
To remove chlorophyll using water alone.
To add starch that was absent from the leaf.
objectives.explanation: Boiling stops ongoing cellular processes; the later ethanol step removes chlorophyll.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: A plant supplied with too little magnesium may develop yellow leaves because magnesium is needed for
options: the chlorophyll molecule.
the cellulose molecule as its only element.
the conversion of every root into a flower.
the formation of animal haemoglobin in leaves.
objectives.explanation: Magnesium is part of chlorophyll, so deficiency can impair pigment production and photosynthesis.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: Which blood component is most directly responsible for antibody production?
options: Platelets.
Red blood cells.
Dissolved urea.
Certain lymphocytes.
objectives.explanation: B lymphocytes can differentiate into plasma cells that secrete antibodies; platelets mainly support clotting.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: What is the main consequence of many stomata closing during a hot, dry afternoon?
options: All xylem vessels change into phloem.
The roots immediately stop absorbing every mineral ion.
Water loss is reduced, but carbon dioxide entry may also be restricted.
Both water loss and carbon dioxide entry must increase.
objectives.explanation: Stomata provide routes for water vapour loss and carbon dioxide uptake, creating a trade-off when they close.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: Which statement correctly compares nervous and hormonal communication?
options: Every hormone acts equally on every cell.
Nerve impulses travel along neurones, whereas hormones are carried to target tissues in blood.
Hormones move only inside motor neurones.
Nerve impulses are carried only in red blood cells.
objectives.explanation: The pathways differ; hormones act on cells with suitable receptors and need not affect every tissue equally.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: Which floral feature is most typical of wind pollination?
options: Large exposed feathery stigmas.
Heavy sticky pollen produced only in tiny quantities.
A closed stigma inaccessible to air.
A strong scent that is the sole mechanism of pollen transfer.
objectives.explanation: Feathery exposed stigmas provide a large surface to catch airborne pollen.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: Which difference is an example of environmental variation rather than a directly inherited blood-group difference?
options: ABO blood group.
An inherited allele for haemoglobin structure.
The X or Y chromosome inherited in a sperm cell.
A scar formed after a cut.
objectives.explanation: A scar results from an acquired injury and repair; ABO blood-group alleles are inherited.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: What is the ecological role of decomposers in a woodland?
options: They prevent every nutrient from re-entering soil.
They convert all animals directly into living trees.
They break down dead organic matter and help return nutrients to the environment.
They create sunlight from mineral salts.
objectives.explanation: Decomposition recycles nutrients; energy flows through the system and is not recycled in the same manner.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: Why should a mark-release-recapture study allow time for marked animals to mix before recapture?
options: To prevent any marked animal from being caught again.
To make marked animals more representative of the population available for sampling.
To ensure every marked animal leaves the habitat permanently.
To make marks alter survival rates.
objectives.explanation: Poor mixing can distort the marked fraction in the recapture sample and bias the estimate.

objectives.subject: Biology
objectives.prompt: A cactus has reduced leaves and a thick waxy surface. These features are most directly associated with
options: limiting water loss in dry habitats.
maximising uncontrolled evaporation.
absorbing food directly from animal blood.
eliminating the need for cellular respiration.
objectives.explanation: Reduced leaf area and a waxy cuticle reduce evaporative loss, helping conserve water.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: Which method best separates a mixture of ethanol and water into fractions enriched in each liquid?
options: Filtration through ordinary paper.
Magnetic separation.
Separating-funnel drainage of two layers.
Fractional distillation.
objectives.explanation: The miscible liquids have different volatilities; repeated vaporisation and condensation improve separation. This does not imply that simple fractional distillation produces unlimited-purity ethanol.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: A dye sample gives two distinct spots during paper chromatography in a suitable solvent. What conclusion is supported?
options: Each spot must represent a chemical element.
The dye contains exactly two atoms.
It contains at least two components separated under those conditions.
It is certainly one pure compound.
objectives.explanation: Distinct spots indicate separable components. A single spot, by contrast, would not always prove purity because substances may co-migrate.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: How many moles are present in 11 g of carbon(IV) oxide? Use C = 12 and O = 16.
options: 44 mol
0.25 mol
0.5 mol
4 mol
objectives.explanation: Molar mass CO₂ = 12+2(16) = 44 g mol⁻¹; amount = 11/44 = 0.25 mol.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: For N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃, 2 mol N₂ is mixed with 3 mol H₂. What is the maximum amount of NH₃, assuming complete reaction?
options: 2 mol
1 mol
3 mol
4 mol
objectives.explanation: The 3 mol of hydrogen reacts with only 1 mol of nitrogen to form 2 mol ammonia. Hydrogen limits the yield; nitrogen remains in excess.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: At constant temperature, a fixed amount of ideal gas is compressed to half its original volume. Its pressure
options: halves.
remains unchanged.
becomes zero.
doubles.
objectives.explanation: Boyle’s law gives PV = constant for a fixed gas amount at constant temperature.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: Why does a gas diffuse faster at a higher temperature, other conditions equal?
options: Its particles stop random motion.
Its molecules all acquire the same velocity.
Its particles have higher average kinetic energy.
Its individual molecules become heavier.
objectives.explanation: Higher average particle speeds increase the rate of spreading; heating does not require each molecule to gain mass.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: An atom has electron arrangement 2,8,1. What is the most likely ion formed in a simple ionic compound?
options: An electrically neutral ion with no electron change.
A singly charged positive ion.
A singly charged negative ion.
A doubly charged negative ion.
objectives.explanation: Loss of the outer electron leaves a stable filled outer shell and a +1 charge.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: Why does solid sodium chloride not conduct electricity while molten sodium chloride does?
options: Its ions are fixed in the solid lattice but mobile in the liquid.
Melting converts every ion to a free electron.
The solid contains no charged particles.
Only neutral sodium atoms carry the current in the liquid.
objectives.explanation: Electrical conduction requires mobile charged particles; melting allows ions to move.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: A catalyst increases reaction rate mainly by
options: raising the equilibrium yield in every reversible reaction.
increasing the enthalpy of every product permanently.
being completely consumed as the limiting reagent.
providing a pathway with lower activation energy.
objectives.explanation: A catalyst changes the reaction pathway and is regenerated; it does not change the reaction’s overall enthalpy difference.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: A reaction releases heat to the surroundings at constant pressure. Which sign describes its enthalpy change for the reacting system?
options: Always zero.
Undefined because energy is destroyed.
Negative.
Positive in every case.
objectives.explanation: For an exothermic reaction, the system’s enthalpy decreases as heat is released.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: A strong monoprotic acid has concentration 1.0 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³ and is fully dissociated. Neglect water’s contribution. What is its pH?
objectives.explanation: The hydrogen-ion concentration is 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³, so pH = −log₁₀(10⁻³) = 3.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: For N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), what is the equilibrium effect of increasing pressure by reducing volume at constant temperature?
options: The equilibrium shifts towards ammonia.
The equilibrium shifts towards the four-mole reactant side.
The equilibrium constant changes solely because volume is reduced.
Pressure cannot affect any gaseous equilibrium.
objectives.explanation: The product side has fewer gas moles: two rather than four. Increased pressure favours that side.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: In Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu, which species is oxidised?
options: Cu²⁺.
Cu metal after it is formed.
Neither reactant because no oxygen is written.
Zn.
objectives.explanation: Zinc loses two electrons to form Zn²⁺; loss of electrons is oxidation.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: Which functional group identifies an alcohol such as ethanol?
options: A carbon-carbon triple bond alone.
An ionic chloride ion alone.
A hydroxyl group bonded to a saturated carbon atom.
A carboxyl group, −COOH.
objectives.explanation: The alcohol group is −OH attached to a saturated carbon; a carboxyl group identifies a carboxylic acid instead.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: Bromine water is decolourised rapidly by ethene without ultraviolet light. What process accounts for this?
options: Complete combustion with no oxygen supply.
Addition across the carbon-carbon double bond.
Neutralisation of an alkali by ethene.
Formation of an ionic metal lattice.
objectives.explanation: Ethene is unsaturated and undergoes addition; substitution of methane normally requires different conditions.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: A mixture contains sand and sodium chloride. Which sequence recovers dry sand and dry salt separately?
options: Add water, filter, then evaporate or crystallise the filtrate and dry the products.
Filter the dry mixture once.
Add water and discard the filtrate.
Heat the dry mixture until sand sublimes.
objectives.explanation: Salt dissolves but sand does not. Filtration separates sand; removal of water recovers salt.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: Isotopes of the same element differ in their number of
options: protons.
nuclei per atom.
electron shells in every neutral atom.
neutrons.
objectives.explanation: They share a proton number but have different neutron numbers and hence different mass numbers.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: Why does graphite conduct electricity along its layers?
options: Every electron is completely immobile.
It contains liquid copper between all layers.
It has delocalised electrons that can move through the structure.
Its carbon atoms move freely as ions in the solid.
objectives.explanation: Some electrons are not confined to individual bonds and can carry charge, unlike mobile ions in a melt.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: A sealed rigid container of gas is heated. Why does its pressure generally rise?
options: Heating converts all particles to vacuum.
Particles collide with the walls more frequently and with greater average momentum change.
The container necessarily doubles its volume.
Particles lose all kinetic energy.
objectives.explanation: At fixed volume, greater average kinetic energy increases the force exerted per area through wall collisions.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: Powdered calcium carbonate reacts faster than equal-mass large lumps with excess dilute acid because the powder
options: offers a larger total surface area for collisions.
has a different atomic number.
always has a lower molar mass.
changes the acid into a catalyst.
objectives.explanation: More exposed reacting surface increases the opportunity for effective collisions under comparable conditions.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: Which observation is expected when dilute acid reacts with a carbonate?
options: A gas that relights a glowing splint.
Formation of hydrogen as the only gaseous product.
No possible gas release under any conditions.
Effervescence of a gas that turns limewater milky.
objectives.explanation: Carbonates react with acids to release CO₂, which forms a calcium carbonate precipitate in limewater.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: What is the oxidation number of sulfur in SO₄²⁻?
objectives.explanation: Four oxygen atoms contribute −8; sulfur must be +6 for the total to be −2.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: During electrolysis of molten lead(II) bromide with inert electrodes, what forms at the cathode?
options: Hydrogen from water.
Lead metal.
Bromine.
Oxygen from water.
objectives.explanation: Pb²⁺ ions gain electrons at the negative cathode: Pb²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Pb.

objectives.subject: Chemistry
objectives.prompt: Which product pair is expected from complete combustion of pure propane in excess oxygen?
options: Carbon dioxide and water.
Carbon monoxide and hydrogen only.
Sodium carbonate and water.
Nitrogen and chlorine.
objectives.explanation: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon converts its carbon to CO₂ and hydrogen to H₂O.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: Which pair consists entirely of SI base quantities?
options: Energy and speed.
Mass and electric current.
Force and mass.
Pressure and time.
objectives.explanation: Mass and electric current are base quantities; force, pressure, energy and speed are derived.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: A ruler has 1 mm divisions and a length is read to the nearest division. Which reported length suggests unjustified precision for a single direct reading?
options: 123 mm
objectives.explanation: A reading to the nearest millimetre corresponds to 0.1 cm, so three decimal places in centimetres are not justified by that reading.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: A runner completes one lap of a circular track and returns to the starting point. Which statement is correct?
options: Both distance and displacement must be zero.
Displacement equals the circumference in every direction.
Distance is negative because the runner returns.
Distance travelled is positive but displacement is zero.
objectives.explanation: Distance measures the path length; displacement depends only on the change in position.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: A trolley increases its velocity uniformly from 2 m s⁻¹ to 14 m s⁻¹ in 4 s along a straight line. Find its acceleration.
options: 4 m s⁻²
12 m s⁻²
3 m s⁻²
0.5 m s⁻²
objectives.explanation: Acceleration = (14−2)/4 = 3 m s⁻².

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: A 6 N force and an 8 N force act at right angles on a body. What is the magnitude of their resultant?
options: 2 N
objectives.explanation: For perpendicular forces, R² = 6²+8² = 100, so R = 10 N.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: A pump raises 50 kg of water through 6 m in 10 s. Neglect losses and take g = 10 m s⁻². What useful power is required?
objectives.explanation: Useful power = mgh/t = 50×10×6/10 = 300 W.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: Which statement correctly applies conservation of energy to a braking bicycle?
options: All kinetic energy disappears from the universe.
The brakes create energy from nothing.
The bicycle must gain gravitational potential energy on every level road.
Some kinetic energy is transferred to thermal energy in the brakes and surroundings.
objectives.explanation: The bicycle’s kinetic energy decreases, but energy is transferred rather than destroyed.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: Why can a metal spoon feel colder than a wooden spoon at the same room temperature?
options: Wood contains no thermal energy.
Temperature is measured only by touch.
Metal transfers thermal energy away from the hand more rapidly.
The metal must have a lower temperature in every room.
objectives.explanation: Thermal conductivity affects the rate of energy flow; the sensation does not prove a lower initial temperature.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: How much energy heats 0.5 kg of water by 20 °C? Take specific heat capacity as 4,200 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ and neglect losses.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: A wave travels at 240 m s⁻¹ with frequency 60 Hz. What is its wavelength?
options: 4 m
objectives.explanation: From v = fλ, wavelength = 240/60 = 4 m.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: Why can sound not travel through an ideal vacuum?
options: Sound requires only an electric field.
Every vacuum absorbs light but transmits all sound.
Sound waves contain stationary material particles that create themselves.
Sound requires a material medium for mechanical disturbance.
objectives.explanation: Sound propagates through particle interactions; an ideal vacuum has no material medium.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: A ray passes obliquely from air into glass. Its speed decreases. Relative to the normal, the transmitted ray generally
options: must travel along the surface.
is converted entirely into sound.
bends towards the normal.
bends away from the normal.
objectives.explanation: Entering a medium with higher refractive index reduces speed and decreases the angle to the normal.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: A 12 V battery is connected across a 4 Ω resistor. Treat both as ideal. What current flows?
options: 3 A
8 A
objectives.explanation: Ohm’s law gives I = V/R = 12/4 = 3 A.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: Two identical lamps are connected in parallel across an ideal battery. If one branch is opened, the other lamp
options: continues to receive the same battery voltage.
must go out because all circuits are series circuits.
receives zero potential difference.
has its resistance automatically doubled.
objectives.explanation: The remaining parallel branch still spans the battery terminals. With an ideal battery its voltage is unchanged.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: A magnet is held stationary inside a stationary coil. With no other changing fields, why is no sustained emf induced?
options: A magnetic field cannot pass through a coil.
All magnets have zero field when near copper.
Induction requires a chemical reaction inside every wire.
The magnetic flux linkage through the coil is not changing.
objectives.explanation: Faraday’s law relates induced emf to the rate of change of flux linkage, not simply the presence of a magnetic field.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: Which physical quantity has the SI unit pascal?
options: Electric charge.
Frequency.
Pressure.
Power.
objectives.explanation: A pascal is one newton per square metre, the SI unit of pressure.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: A book rests on a horizontal table. Which pair is a Newton’s third-law interaction pair?
options: The mass of the book and its weight.
The force of the book on the table and the force of the table on the book.
The book’s weight and the normal force acting on that same book.
Two separate forces both exerted only on the Earth.
objectives.explanation: Third-law forces arise from one interaction and act on different bodies; weight and normal force on the same book are not such a pair.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: A machine receives 800 J and delivers 600 J of useful output. Its efficiency is
objectives.explanation: Efficiency = useful output/input × 100% = 600/800×100% = 75%.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: During steady boiling of pure water at constant pressure, added heat mainly
options: raises the temperature without limit while liquid remains.
reduces the mass of every water molecule.
eliminates all intermolecular forces in the remaining liquid.
provides latent heat for the liquid-to-vapour change.
objectives.explanation: Energy is used in the phase change while temperature remains at the boiling point under these conditions.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: Which change increases the pitch of a sound in the same medium?
options: Decreasing its frequency.
Increasing only the source’s loudness at fixed frequency.
Increasing its frequency.
Increasing only its amplitude.
objectives.explanation: Pitch is primarily related to frequency; amplitude relates mainly to loudness.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: What type of image is formed by a plane mirror?
options: Virtual and always twice the object’s size.
Virtual, upright and the same size as the object.
Real and always smaller than the object.
Real and upside down.
objectives.explanation: The image appears behind the mirror at the same perpendicular distance and cannot be projected onto a screen directly.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: Why is a fuse wire placed in series with the live conductor of an appliance?
options: It can melt and break the circuit if current becomes excessive.
It stores all excess charge without heating.
It guarantees that the appliance uses no power.
It increases current to any value the appliance requests.
objectives.explanation: The series fuse carries the appliance current and interrupts the live supply when its rating is exceeded sufficiently.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: For a uniform wire of fixed material and temperature, which change increases resistance?
options: Increasing cross-sectional area at fixed length.
Reducing length at fixed area.
Using a shorter and thicker piece of the same wire.
Increasing length while keeping cross-sectional area constant.
objectives.explanation: R = ρL/A, so resistance rises with length when resistivity and area are unchanged.

objectives.subject: Physics
objectives.prompt: Which change reverses the force on a current-carrying wire in a fixed magnetic field, if the wire is initially perpendicular to the field?
options: Increase only the wire’s mass.
Reverse both current and magnetic field together.
Reverse the current direction only.
Double the current without reversing it.
objectives.explanation: The magnetic-force direction reverses when current reverses while the field direction stays fixed.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Choose the correct completion: My brother and I ___ the classroom every Friday.
options: cleaning
has cleaned
clean
cleans
objectives.explanation: The plural subject my brother and I takes clean in the simple present.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Choose the correct past tense: Yesterday, the gardener ___ a deep hole.
options: digging
dug
digged
dig
objectives.explanation: Dug is the past tense of dig; the time word yesterday calls for a past form.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Which word correctly replaces the repeated name? “I met Amina and gave Amina the book.”
options: her
she
hers
herselfs
objectives.explanation: Amina is the object of gave, so the object pronoun her is appropriate.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Select the sentence with the correct possessive form for one girl.
options: The girls bag’s is blue.
The girls’ bag is blue.
The girl bag is blue.
The girl’s bag is blue.
objectives.explanation: An apostrophe followed by s marks possession by one girl.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Choose the word that means nearly the same as enormous.
options: Narrow
Empty
Huge
Tiny
objectives.explanation: Enormous and huge both describe very great size.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: In “The path was slippery after the rain,” slippery means
options: closed because it has no end.
difficult to walk on without sliding.
covered with sharp stones only.
very wide and completely dry.
objectives.explanation: Rain can make a surface smooth and wet so that feet slide on it.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Choose the opposite of generous.
options: Stingy
Helpful
Kind
Cheerful
objectives.explanation: A generous person gives freely; a stingy person is unwilling to give or share.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Which sentence is a polite request?
options: Close it now, you fool!
The window was closed yesterday.
What a beautiful window!
Could you please close the window?
objectives.explanation: It asks for an action courteously using could and please.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Complete the sentence: The cat hid ___ the table during the storm.
options: although
quickly
under
because
objectives.explanation: Under expresses a position below the table. The other choices do not fit the intended location or sentence structure.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Choose the correct conjunction: Tunde carried an umbrella ___ it was raining.
options: although
because
unless
until
objectives.explanation: Because introduces the reason for carrying the umbrella.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: “Where is my ruler?” asked Ada.
“Where is my ruler.” asked Ada?
“Where is my ruler” asked Ada.
Where is my ruler,? asked Ada.
objectives.explanation: The spoken question has a question mark inside the closing quotation mark, followed by the reporting clause.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Choose the correct comparative form: This road is ___ than the narrow lane.
options: widest
more wider
most wide
wider
objectives.explanation: The comparative of wide is wider and is used with than.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Which word is an adverb in “The pupils waited patiently outside”?
options: the
waited
patiently
pupils
objectives.explanation: Patiently describes how the pupils waited; it modifies the verb.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Complete the sentence: Each of the baskets ___ a label.
options: were
has
have
are
objectives.explanation: Each is singular, even though baskets is plural inside the following phrase.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Which sentence describes an action happening now?
options: The carpenter is repairing the chair.
The carpenter repaired the chair last week.
The carpenter will repair the chair tomorrow.
The carpenter had repaired the chair before noon.
objectives.explanation: Is repairing is the present continuous form, which can describe an action in progress.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Where did Kene find the bag?
options: Inside his classroom.
Behind the library.
In Mary’s house.
Beside the school gate.
objectives.explanation: The opening sentence states the location directly.
objectives.passage: On Monday, Kene found a small bag beside the school gate. It contained a lunch box and a notebook, but no money. He wanted to identify the owner, so he looked at the name written inside the notebook. The name was partly covered by a sticker. Instead of guessing, Kene took the bag to the school office and explained where he had found it. The secretary announced that a bag had been found without describing everything inside. Later, a pupil named Mary came to the office. She described the lunch box and the notebook accurately before the secretary returned the bag to her.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Why could Kene not read the whole name in the notebook?
options: The bag contained only food.
Mary had erased every word.
A sticker covered part of it.
The notebook had no pages.
objectives.explanation: The passage says the written name was partly hidden by a sticker.
objectives.passage: On Monday, Kene found a small bag beside the school gate. It contained a lunch box and a notebook, but no money. Later, a pupil named Mary came to the office. She described the lunch box and the notebook accurately before the secretary returned the bag to her.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Why was it sensible for the secretary to avoid announcing every item in the bag?
options: The office wanted to keep every lost bag forever.
The owner could later describe the contents as evidence.
It would make the bag disappear.
Nobody was allowed to own a notebook.
objectives.explanation: Mary’s accurate description helped the secretary check her claim. Publicly revealing every item would make this check less useful.

He wanted to identify the owner, so he looked at the name written inside the notebook. The name was partly covered by a sticker. Later, a pupil named Mary came to the office. She described the lunch box and the notebook accurately before the secretary returned the bag to her.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Which quality does Kene show by taking the bag to the office?
options: Honesty.
Greed.
Cruelty.
Laziness.
objectives.explanation: He tried to return someone else’s property instead of keeping it.

Later, a pupil named Mary came to the office. She described the lunch box and the notebook accurately before the secretary returned the bag to her.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Which statement is supported by the passage about the lost bag?
options: The bag contained a large amount of money.
Kene opened the bag inside Mary’s house.
The secretary knew the owner before the announcement.
Mary identified items that were inside the bag.
objectives.explanation: The final sentences explicitly say she described the lunch box and notebook accurately.

Later, a pupil named Mary came to the office. She described the lunch box and the notebook accurately before the secretary returned the bag to her.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: What was the main difference in the treatment of the two containers?
options: The amount of soil used.
The amount of water supplied.
The amount of light available to them.
The type of seed planted.
objectives.explanation: One container was by a sunny window and the other was in a dark cupboard; soil and watering were kept alike.
objectives.passage: The Primary Six class planted beans in two identical containers. Both containers held the same type and amount of soil, and both received equal amounts of water. The class placed one container near a sunny window and the other in a dark cupboard. After several days, the seedlings in the cupboard were pale and thin, while those near the window were greener. The pupils recorded the changes instead of pulling up the seedlings each day. Their teacher reminded them that a fair comparison required more than noticing one difference: they also needed to keep the other important conditions alike. The class decided to repeat the investigation before writing its final report.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Why did the pupils keep the soil and water amounts the same?
options: To make both containers completely dark.
To make the effect of light easier to compare fairly.
To prove that plants never need water.
To prevent any seeds from germinating.
objectives.explanation: Keeping other relevant conditions alike reduces alternative explanations for the observed differences.
objectives.passage: The Primary Six class planted beans in two identical containers. Both containers held the same type and amount of soil, and both received equal amounts of water. The class placed one container near a sunny window and the other in a dark cupboard. After several days, the seedlings in the cupboard were pale and thin, while those near the window were greener. The pupils recorded the changes instead of pulling up the seedlings each day. Their teacher reminded them that a fair comparison required more than noticing one difference: they also needed to keep the other important conditions alike. The class decided to repeat the investigation before writing its final report.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Which description matches the seedlings kept in the cupboard?
options: Pale and thin.
Greener than those by the window.
Covered in ripe bean pods.
Identical in colour to the sunny seedlings.
objectives.explanation: These are the two observed features stated in the passage.
objectives.passage: The Primary Six class planted beans in two identical containers. Both containers held the same type and amount of soil, and both received equal amounts of water. The class decided to repeat the investigation before writing its final report.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: Why was recording changes preferable to pulling up the seedlings each day?
options: It guaranteed that no seedling would ever die.
It made sunlight unnecessary.
It changed the seeds into a different species.
It allowed observation without repeatedly disturbing their growth.
objectives.explanation: Removing seedlings could damage or disturb them, creating another difference in the investigation.
objectives.passage: The Primary Six class planted beans in two identical containers. Both containers held the same type and amount of soil, and both received equal amounts of water. The class decided to repeat the investigation before writing its final report.

objectives.subject: English Studies
objectives.prompt: What does the class’s decision to repeat the investigation suggest?
options: They believed a report should contain no evidence.
They wanted to change every condition at once.
They wanted to check whether the result would occur again.
They had decided to hide all observations.
objectives.explanation: Repeating a fair investigation helps assess whether an observation is consistent rather than relying on one trial.

The class decided to repeat the investigation before writing its final report.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: Why do green plants need sunlight?
options: It provides the carbon atoms in glucose directly.
It supplies energy for making food during photosynthesis.
It replaces all water absorbed by roots.
It makes soil unnecessary for every kind of plant.
objectives.explanation: Light provides energy; it is not a mineral taken up by the roots.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: Which part of a flowering plant takes in most water from the soil?
options: Roots.
Petals.
Fruits.
Anthers.
objectives.explanation: Roots, particularly their root hairs, absorb water from soil.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: Which sequence shows the usual main stages in a butterfly’s life cycle?
options: Egg → pupa → larva → adult.
Adult → seed → pupa → egg.
Larva → egg → adult → pupa.
Egg → larva → pupa → adult.
objectives.explanation: A butterfly undergoes complete metamorphosis with a caterpillar larva and a pupal stage.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: Which meal supplies both an energy-giving staple and a protein-rich food?
options: Water and salt only.
Palm oil and sugar only.
Rice and beans.
Plain sugar and sweets only.
objectives.explanation: Rice supplies mainly carbohydrate, while beans contribute protein as well as other nutrients.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: Why are teeth of different shapes useful?
options: Tooth shape has no connection with chewing.
Different shapes help cut, tear and grind food.
Every tooth is used only to taste sweetness.
Teeth make food without chewing.
objectives.explanation: Incisors, canines and broad back teeth have different forms suited to different actions.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: Which organism is a producer in a simple pond food chain?
options: Green algae.
A fish that eats insects.
A frog that eats flies.
A snail feeding on algae.
objectives.explanation: Green algae can make organic food using light and provide food for consumers.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: Why should a school avoid removing every flowering plant from its garden?
options: Flowers prevent all insects from reproducing.
Every flower makes the soil poisonous.
Only stones can support living things.
Some insects depend on flowers for nectar and pollen.
objectives.explanation: Flowering plants provide resources for pollinating insects and help support garden food relationships.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: Which material property makes clear glass suitable for a window?
options: It is always flexible like rubber.
It dissolves immediately in rainwater.
It lets visible light pass through.
It absorbs all visible light.
objectives.explanation: Transparency allows light through while the solid pane provides a physical barrier.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: Which change is usually reversible by cooling?
options: Rusting an iron nail.
Melting candle wax without burning it.
Burning a sheet of paper.
Cooking an egg.
objectives.explanation: Melted wax can solidify when cooled; burning produces new substances and is not simply reversed by cooling.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: Wet clothes dry on a line mainly because water
options: evaporates into the surrounding air.
turns into sand.
is destroyed by moving air.
freezes and remains inside the cloth.
objectives.explanation: Evaporation changes liquid water to water vapour at the cloth surface.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: How can a learner separate iron filings from dry sand most easily?
options: Use a torch to shine light through it.
Add more dry sand.
Use a ruler to measure the mixture.
Use a magnet.
objectives.explanation: Iron filings are attracted to a magnet while ordinary sand is not strongly attracted.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: Why is a plastic coating used around many electric wires?
options: It turns electricity into drinking water.
It guarantees that damaged wires are always safe.
It is an insulator that helps prevent contact with the conducting metal.
It carries more current than the metal core.
objectives.explanation: The coating limits unwanted current paths and protects users from touching the live conductor.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: Water droplets form on the outside of a cold bottle. Where does this water mainly come from?
options: All plastic turns into water when cooled.
Water vapour in the surrounding air condenses on the cold surface.
Water passes directly through intact glass.
The bottle creates new hydrogen and oxygen atoms.
objectives.explanation: The cold surface cools moist air, allowing vapour to become liquid droplets.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: A wheelbarrow helps a gardener carry a heavy load. Which simple machine is involved when the handles are lifted about the wheel?
options: A lever.
An electric generator.
