A thermometer.
A prism.
objectives.explanation: The wheel acts as a pivot, the load is between it and the applied effort, so the wheelbarrow works as a second-class lever.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: Which arrangement is necessary for a small torch bulb to light from a suitable cell?
options: A gap in every connecting wire.
Both wires attached only to the same cell terminal.
A bulb connected only to a dry wooden stick.
A complete conducting path between the cell terminals through the bulb.
objectives.explanation: A closed circuit allows current to pass through the filament or lamp element.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: Why does a shadow form behind an opaque object?
options: Light bends around every object completely.
Shadows form only when no light source exists.
The object blocks light travelling from the source.
The object produces darkness as a liquid.
objectives.explanation: Light cannot pass through the opaque object, leaving a region with less direct light behind it.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: Which action increases friction between a shoe and a smooth floor?
options: Removing all contact between the shoe and floor.
Using a sole with a suitable rough tread.
Polishing the sole until it is very smooth.
Adding oil to the walking surface.
objectives.explanation: A suitable tread can improve grip compared with a smooth sole on the same surface.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: What energy change occurs when a battery-operated fan runs?
options: Stored chemical energy is transferred into electrical energy and movement, with some heating.
Movement creates all the battery chemicals from nothing.
Light is the only possible output.
No energy transfer takes place.
objectives.explanation: The battery supplies electrical energy from chemical processes, and the motor drives the blades.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: Why is a ramp useful when loading a crate onto a platform?
options: It removes the crate’s mass permanently.
It makes gravity act upwards.
It always needs zero effort.
It allows a smaller lifting force to act over a longer distance.
objectives.explanation: A ramp trades a longer path for reduced force in an ideal case; it does not remove the energy needed to raise the crate.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: Which habit helps conserve water at school?
options: Ignoring a leaking tank for a term.
Pouring clean water onto an empty road each morning.
Closing a tap fully after use and reporting leaks.
Leaving a tap running during the whole break.
objectives.explanation: Stopping unnecessary flow and repairing leaks reduce avoidable water loss.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: Why should used batteries be kept out of a school’s compost heap?
options: They always improve soil in any quantity.
They are not compostable plant material and may release harmful substances.
They turn every leaf into a battery.
They are needed by every earthworm as food.
objectives.explanation: Compost is made from suitable biodegradable organic material; batteries need an appropriate collection or disposal route.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: A pupil wants to protect a private account. Which choice is best?
options: Use a strong password and keep it private.
Post the password on the classroom wall.
Give the password to strangers online.
Use the public school name as every account’s only password.
objectives.explanation: A strong private password helps prevent unauthorised access; sharing it removes that protection.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: Which tool is most appropriate for measuring the length of a classroom wall?
options: A clinical thermometer.
A weighing scale.
A stopwatch.
A measuring tape.
objectives.explanation: A measuring tape can measure a length of several metres conveniently.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: Why is burning mixed plastic waste near classrooms a poor choice?
options: It guarantees better air quality.
It prevents all future waste from being created.
It can pollute the air and expose people to smoke.
It produces only clean oxygen.
objectives.explanation: Burning mixed plastics can release pollutants; reducing waste and using suitable collection are preferable.

objectives.subject: Basic Science and Technology
objectives.prompt: A seedling in a reused container stays waterlogged after watering. Which design change is most useful?
options: Replace all the soil with engine oil.
Add suitable drainage holes and place a tray underneath.
Seal every opening permanently.
Wrap the whole seedling in an airtight bag.
objectives.explanation: Drainage allows excess water to leave rather than remain around the roots; a tray can collect the runoff.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: A manufacturer produces shoes, while another business transports them to shops. Which statement best distinguishes their roles?
options: Transport must manufacture the leather before it can move shoes.
Only physical manufacturing can add any utility.
The transporter owns every shop that receives shoes.
Manufacturing creates the shoes; transport helps make them available where buyers need them.
objectives.explanation: Production and commercial aids are related; transport helps overcome the barrier of place.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: Which activity belongs to primary production?
options: Selling desks in a showroom.
Advertising a furniture delivery service.
Harvesting timber from a managed forest.
Making desks from timber.
objectives.explanation: Primary production obtains natural resources; furniture manufacture is secondary production.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: A factory divides assembly into specialised tasks. Which disadvantage may arise if workers learn only one narrow task?
options: The factory no longer needs coordination.
They may find it harder to move to other roles when technology changes.
Every worker automatically becomes equally skilled in all occupations.
Training ceases to have any value.
objectives.explanation: Narrow specialisation can restrict adaptability even when it improves efficiency in the current process.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: Which feature most clearly distinguishes a consumer cooperative’s purpose from that of a conventional investor-owned retailer?
options: It is organised to serve its member-consumers through their jointly owned enterprise.
It is necessarily owned by one government minister.
It is prohibited from buying goods for resale in every country.
It has no members and no governance.
objectives.explanation: A consumer cooperative’s members are also its intended users, rather than ownership being defined only by outside investment.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: Two firms combine operations to form one business through a merger. What is a possible commercial motive?
options: Making all demand disappear.
Ensuring that integration requires no planning.
Automatically eliminating every business risk.
Combining complementary resources and reducing duplicated costs.
objectives.explanation: A merger may seek synergies, although these are not guaranteed.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: A sole proprietor wants to preserve full decision-making control. Which possible trade-off should be recognised?
options: Control removes the need to keep business records.
A sole proprietor can never employ a manager.
The owner may have a narrower pool of finance and management skills than a business with several owners.
Sole ownership always guarantees the largest possible capital base.
objectives.explanation: Control can be retained at the cost of access to other owners’ funds and expertise.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: A producer sells fresh bread directly to nearby households each morning. Which factor most strongly supports a short distribution channel?
options: Households can buy only from foreign wholesalers.
The product is perishable and customers are close to the producer.
Bread becomes less perishable when intermediaries increase.
A long channel is compulsory for every locally sold product.
objectives.explanation: Short channels can reduce time before consumption when distance and customer reach permit.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: A seller issues a credit note after accepting a customer’s return of damaged goods. What does the note normally communicate?
options: The amount owed by that customer is being reduced.
The customer must pay the original invoice twice.
The seller has made a new loan unrelated to the return.
The returned goods are automatically exports.
objectives.explanation: The seller acknowledges a reduction of the original charge for accepted returns or allowances.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: What is the main function of a pro forma invoice sent before a confirmed sale?
options: Prove that cash has already been received in every case.
Replace every transport document.
Certify that a bank has insured the buyer’s warehouse.
Provide a preliminary statement of proposed goods and charges.
objectives.explanation: A pro forma invoice supplies indicative transaction details; it is not the same as a receipt confirming payment.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: A country imports goods and later exports those same goods without substantial processing. This is described as
options: retail trade with no border movement.
primary production.
entrepôt trade.
barter within one household.
objectives.explanation: Entrepôt trade involves importing for re-export rather than domestic consumption or substantial manufacture.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: Which source of finance is most directly generated inside a profitable business?
options: A supplier’s credit facility.
Retained profits.
A new bank loan.
A new outside investor’s contribution.
objectives.explanation: Retained profits are earnings kept in the business rather than distributed; bank loans and new outside investment are external sources.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: A shop has current assets of ₦480,000 and current liabilities of ₦310,000. What is working capital?
objectives.explanation: Working capital is current assets minus current liabilities: ₦480,000−₦310,000 = ₦170,000.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: Why is financing a long-lived factory mainly with immediately repayable short-term borrowing potentially risky?
options: A long-lived asset always generates its full purchase cost on the first day.
Short-term borrowing can never carry any repayment obligation.
The factory’s physical life automatically postpones the loan due date.
The debt may fall due before the asset generates enough cash to repay it.
objectives.explanation: A maturity mismatch can create refinancing and liquidity pressure despite the asset’s long-term usefulness.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: Under the principle of indemnity, the general aim of a valid property-insurance claim is to
options: transfer ownership of every insured asset before any loss.
remove every policy condition.
restore the insured’s financial position for the covered loss, within policy terms.
guarantee profit greater than the loss in every claim.
objectives.explanation: Indemnity compensates loss rather than providing a profit merely because damage occurred.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: A business insures goods for transit. Why should it disclose material information requested by the insurer honestly?
options: An insurance proposal is unrelated to the risks being insured.
The information affects the insurer’s assessment and acceptance of the risk.
Disclosure makes all goods impossible to damage.
Only favourable information can ever affect risk assessment.
objectives.explanation: Material disclosure supports the insurance principle of utmost good faith; it is not a guarantee that every possible event is covered.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: Which transport mode is generally most suitable for moving a continuous large flow of crude oil between fixed connected points?
options: Pipeline.
Passenger bicycles.
Hand-carried parcels.
Ordinary postal letters.
objectives.explanation: Pipelines suit fluid movement between connected points, subject to the infrastructure and route.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: Why might a retailer choose air freight for a small consignment of urgently needed, high-value spare parts?
options: Air freight is always the cheapest mode for every heavy bulk commodity.
All air shipments arrive with no handling or route constraints.
Urgency has no relevance to mode choice.
Saving time can justify a higher transport cost relative to the consignment’s value and urgency.
objectives.explanation: Mode choice depends on time, value, size and cost rather than lowest freight charge alone.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: What commercial problem does warehousing chiefly help solve when production is seasonal but sales occur throughout the year?
options: The need to manufacture all goods in the warehouse itself.
The impossibility of maintaining inventory records.
The timing gap between production and consumption.
The absence of every form of consumer demand.
objectives.explanation: Storage can hold output until it is needed, subject to cost and preservation constraints.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: A business asks potential customers which packaging size they prefer before launching a product. This is mainly
options: a bank reconciliation.
market research.
mass advertising.
a finished sales invoice.
objectives.explanation: The business is gathering information to support a marketing decision rather than simply promoting an existing offer.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: A washing-machine supplier provides installation and repair support after purchase. This is an example of
options: after-sales service.
primary extraction.
a customs tariff.
an unpaid import duty.
objectives.explanation: Support after purchase can improve customer experience and confidence in using the product.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: A promotion gives a temporary price reduction to encourage immediate purchases. What distinguishes this from ordinary long-term brand advertising?
options: It guarantees every purchaser becomes loyal permanently.
It eliminates the need to deliver the advertised goods.
It prevents any measurement of sales response.
It is a short-term sales incentive with a direct purchase trigger.
objectives.explanation: Sales promotion commonly uses temporary incentives, while brand advertising may build awareness over a longer period.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: A supervisor assigns a routine purchasing task to an assistant with clear limits. Which principle is illustrated?
options: A merger of all suppliers.
A change from money to barter.
Delegation of authority.
Elimination of accountability.
objectives.explanation: The assistant receives authority for a task, while the supervisor retains responsibility for appropriate oversight.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: Why can an excessively wide span of control create difficulty for a manager?
options: It automatically increases the manager’s available hours.
Too many direct reports can reduce the time available for guidance and supervision.
It always removes every communication channel.
It guarantees that all tasks become identical.
objectives.explanation: The suitable span depends on task complexity and staff capability; there is no universal number for every business.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: A business compares actual monthly sales with its plan and investigates a shortfall. Which management function is most directly involved?
options: Controlling.
Mining.
Sublimation.
Barter.
objectives.explanation: Control compares performance with objectives and supports corrective action.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: A shop receives the same complaint from many customers but records none of them. What is the strongest management weakness?
options: Customer complaints are always proof of fraud.
Keeping records automatically resolves every complaint.
Only large multinational firms can learn from complaints.
The business loses evidence needed to identify and correct a recurring problem.
objectives.explanation: Records can reveal patterns and test whether corrective action works.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: Which statement best describes commerce?
options: Only unpaid household cooking.
Every biological process in a plant.
Activities that facilitate exchange and distribution, including trade and aids to trade.
Only the physical extraction of minerals.
objectives.explanation: Commerce connects buying and selling with enabling services such as transport, finance and communication.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: Why may partners agree their duties and profit-sharing arrangements in writing?
options: To ensure that every partner has exactly the same personal skills.
To clarify expectations and reduce avoidable disputes.
To make all business losses mathematically impossible.
To remove the need for any accounting records.
objectives.explanation: An agreed record can define roles and allocation rules; it does not guarantee no future disagreement.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: A chamber of commerce is generally distinguished from a single-industry trade association because it
options: can represent business interests across several trades within an area.
must manufacture every member’s products.
is identical to a private household savings box.
has no connection with business interests.
objectives.explanation: A chamber has a broader cross-trade remit, while an industry association focuses on a particular trade or sector.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: Which feature characterises a department store rather than a chain of separate shops?
options: Only one narrow product can ever be sold.
Every outlet must have a different unrelated owner.
Goods are sold only to other wholesalers.
Several product departments operate within one large retail establishment.
objectives.explanation: Departments are grouped in one establishment; chain stores consist of multiple outlets under common ownership.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: Why can an intermediary remain useful even when a producer could theoretically contact retailers directly?
options: It necessarily doubles every product’s usefulness without cost.
Only intermediaries can legally speak to consumers in every market.
It may perform storage, breaking bulk and market-contact functions efficiently.
Its functions disappear from the market whenever it is removed.
objectives.explanation: Eliminating an intermediary does not eliminate the functions it performs; another participant must carry them out.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: A buyer pays before goods are dispatched under a cash-with-order arrangement. Which description is correct?
options: Payment can occur only after the goods are resold.
Payment accompanies the order rather than waiting for delivery.
Payment is made only after ten years in every case.
The seller must never receive payment.
objectives.explanation: Cash with order differs from cash on delivery in the timing of payment.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: A business sells 400 units at ₦2,500 each during a period. What is its sales turnover for that period?
objectives.explanation: Turnover here means sales revenue: quantity sold × selling price. It is not profit without cost information.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: Why is a share different from a conventional fixed-interest debenture?
options: Every share is a demand deposit at a commercial bank.
Every debenture makes the holder a retail customer.
Both are always identical to ordinary cash receipts.
A share represents equity ownership, while a debenture normally represents borrowing.
objectives.explanation: Their claims and returns differ; ownership should not be confused with lending.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: What is the main purpose of reinsurance?
options: A bank prints new legal-tender currency.
A retailer cancels every inventory record.
An insurer transfers part of its accepted risk to another insurer.
An insured trader sells damaged goods without disclosure.
objectives.explanation: Reinsurance spreads an insurer’s exposure; it is not the same as a consumer taking out an unrelated second policy.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: Which event is a pure risk rather than a speculative business opportunity?
options: Speculating on a commodity’s future price.
Accidental fire damage to a warehouse.
Buying goods in the hope that market prices rise.
Opening a new branch to seek extra profits.
objectives.explanation: A pure risk involves possible loss or no loss rather than the prospect of profit from taking the risk.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: A supplier sends a detailed written delivery schedule to several branches. What advantage does writing provide?
options: A common record that recipients can refer to and check.
A guarantee that no recipient can misunderstand any word.
Automatic transport of the goods without vehicles.
Removal of every need for confirmation.
objectives.explanation: Written communication can improve consistency and provide evidence, although it does not by itself ensure everyone reads it.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: Why should storage conditions differ for frozen food and bags of cement?
options: All goods need exactly the same temperature and humidity.
Cement is preserved best by soaking it before storage.
Frozen food never changes during storage.
The products deteriorate in different ways and require different protection.
objectives.explanation: Frozen food needs temperature control, while cement must be protected against moisture and contamination.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: Which action changes the place element of the marketing mix?
options: Changing only the advertising slogan.
Reducing only the quoted price.
Adding a convenient collection point near customers.
Changing only the package colour.
objectives.explanation: Place concerns distribution and access, rather than merely changing promotion or product appearance.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: Which advertisement is primarily informative?
options: A promise of guaranteed wealth without stating a product.
A notice stating a new bus route, its stops and its timetable.
A slogan claiming an unnamed product makes everyone famous.
A picture with no service details and only a celebrity endorsement.
objectives.explanation: It supplies service facts that help users make decisions, rather than relying mainly on emotional persuasion.

objectives.subject: Commerce
objectives.prompt: A manager sets an objective but gives staff no deadline or performance measure. What improvement is most useful?
options: Define a realistic timescale and a way to assess achievement.
Replace the objective with an unrelated slogan.
Ban all communication about progress.
Assume effort alone proves that the objective has been achieved.
objectives.explanation: A clear measure and deadline make it possible to monitor progress and evaluate the objective.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: A proprietor pays a child’s personal school fees from the business bank account. Under the business-entity concept, this payment is normally recorded as
options: a trade payable to all customers.
drawings, not a business operating expense.
sales revenue.
factory overhead in every case.
objectives.explanation: The owner’s personal consumption is separated from the business’s expenses.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: Which assumption supports preparing accounts without valuing every asset as if an immediate forced liquidation were planned?
options: Going concern.
Every business closes at the end of each month.
All transactions are ignored until cash is counted.
Owner and business are the same accounting entity.
objectives.explanation: Going concern assumes continuing operation unless evidence indicates otherwise; it does not guarantee permanent survival.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: A service is completed and invoiced before year-end, but the customer pays next month. Under accrual accounting, recognition normally follows
options: only the date the owner spends the money.
the date the customer first heard of the business.
never recognising credit services.
when the service is earned, not merely when cash arrives.
objectives.explanation: Accrual accounting distinguishes earning income from receiving cash.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: An owner injects additional cash capital into a business. Why is this not sales revenue?
options: Capital contributions are always trade discounts.
The cash cannot appear in the business records.
It is an owner contribution rather than income earned from trading.
Every cash receipt must be revenue.
objectives.explanation: Financing by owners increases equity without being revenue from customers.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: Under a periodic inventory system, goods for resale are bought on credit. Which double entry is appropriate?
options: Debit sales; credit cash.
Debit purchases; credit the supplier’s account.
Debit the supplier; credit sales.
Debit drawings; credit purchases.
objectives.explanation: Purchases increase and the amount owed to the supplier is recognised.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: Which source document normally supports recording a credit sale of goods in the sales journal?
options: The sales invoice issued to the customer.
A personal birthday invitation.
A wage time sheet unrelated to the sale.
An uncompleted cheque with no transaction details.
objectives.explanation: A credit-sales invoice provides evidence of the customer, goods and amount charged.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: A business returns goods to a credit supplier, who accepts the return. Under periodic inventory accounting, which entry reduces the debt?
options: Debit sales; credit the supplier.
Debit drawings; credit wages.
Debit purchases; credit cash.
Debit the supplier; credit purchases returns.
objectives.explanation: Debiting the payable reduces what is owed, while purchases returns records the goods sent back.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: Cash is deposited from the till into the business bank account. In a two-column cash book, this is
options: a bad debt written off.
an additional profit from a customer.
a contra entry between cash and bank columns.
a new credit sale.
objectives.explanation: The transfer changes the location of the business’s money but is not income or an expense.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: An imprest petty-cash float is ₦15,000 and valid vouchers total ₦11,200. What reimbursement restores the float, assuming no other differences?
objectives.explanation: The reimbursement equals supported spending, replacing the amount used from the float.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: Goods have list price ₦20,000 less a 10% trade discount. In the buyer’s ordinary purchases records, what amount is initially recorded before any cash discount?
options: ₦20,000 with ₦2,000 posted as cash discount.
₦2,000 as the full purchase.
objectives.explanation: Trade discount is deducted before recording the invoice amount: 20,000×0.90 = 18,000.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: A bank overdraft is normally classified in a basic statement of financial position as
options: sales revenue.
an inventory item.
a reduction of every non-current asset.
a liability.
objectives.explanation: An overdraft represents money owed to the bank rather than a positive cash asset.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: Bank charges appear on the statement but have not been recorded in the cash book. What is the appropriate cash-book update?
options: Debit drawings and credit the customer.
Make no update because all bank-statement items are timing differences.
Debit bank-charges expense and credit bank.
Debit bank and credit sales.
objectives.explanation: The charge reduces the bank asset balance and recognises an expense.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: A credit purchase is completely omitted from both relevant ledger accounts. What is the effect on trial-balance agreement?
options: Agreement proves the omission could not have occurred.
The trial balance can still agree.
The debit total must exceed the credit total by twice the purchase.
The omission automatically creates a cash surplus.
objectives.explanation: Both debit and credit are missing, so equal totals do not prove that every transaction was recorded.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: A new machine’s cost is debited to repairs expense instead of the machine account, with the credit entry correct. This is principally an error of
options: principle.
complete omission.
original-entry transposition affecting both sides equally.
bank timing only.
objectives.explanation: A capital item has been treated as a revenue expense; the debit-credit arithmetic may still balance.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: An allowance for doubtful receivables is increased at year-end. Other things equal, what is the usual effect of the increase?
options: A guaranteed receipt of cash.
An increase in sales units already delivered.
Elimination of every customer debt.
An expense increase and a reduction in net receivables.
objectives.explanation: The increase recognises expected non-collection and reduces the receivable’s net reported amount.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: Why is depreciation not itself a fund of cash set aside for replacing an asset?
options: Depreciation can occur only when cash is paid each year.
Depreciation increases the asset’s physical output automatically.
It is an accounting allocation of cost and does not by itself move cash into a separate fund.
Every depreciation entry automatically opens a funded bank account.
objectives.explanation: Recognising depreciation and saving cash are distinct actions.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: A machine requires an installation charge before it can operate as intended. In a basic historical-cost model, the charge is normally
options: ignored because the machine has already been purchased.
included in the machine’s cost.
treated as the owner’s personal drawings.
deducted from sales discounts.
objectives.explanation: A directly attributable cost of bringing the asset into use forms part of the recorded asset cost.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: What does the current ratio mainly compare?
options: Current assets with current liabilities.
Net profit with sales revenue.
Non-current assets with the number of employees.
Cash sales with advertising slogans.
objectives.explanation: It is a liquidity indicator, not a direct measure of profit margin or inventory units.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: A good is sold for ₦120 after costing ₦90. What is gross profit as a percentage of sales?
objectives.explanation: Gross profit is 30; margin on sales is 30/120×100 = 25%. Mark-up on cost uses a different denominator.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: How can a profitable business still face a cash shortage?
options: A business cannot sell on credit if it makes any profit.
Cash shortages prove every revenue entry is false.
Revenue may have been earned on credit while expenses and purchases require earlier payment.
Accounting profit always equals the bank balance.
objectives.explanation: Profit recognition and cash timing differ, so positive profit does not ensure immediate liquidity.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: In a textbook partnership appropriation account, a partner’s agreed salary is normally treated as
options: a sales return.
an allocation of profit to that partner.
a purchase of inventory from the partner.
a loan repayment to all suppliers.
objectives.explanation: Within this model, partner salary is part of profit appropriation, distinct from an employee’s operating wage.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: Where fixed capital accounts are used for partners, routine drawings and profit shares are normally recorded in
options: partners’ current accounts.
the sales returns journal only.
an inventory quantity card only.
the company’s share-premium account.
objectives.explanation: Current accounts track routine changes while the agreed fixed capital balances remain separate.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: When inventory turnover is defined as cost of sales divided by inventory held, which denominator is most appropriate for a period when both opening and closing figures are available?
options: Closing sales revenue.
Average inventory measured at cost.
Total customer receipts.
The number of employees.
objectives.explanation: Using an average balance at cost aligns the inventory measure with cost of sales and is generally more representative than a single closing balance. The simple mean is an approximation if inventory varies within the period.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: A public-sector accounting report compares expenditure with an authorised budget. What purpose does this serve?
options: Remove the need for supporting documents.
Guarantee that every recorded payment was efficient.
Support accountability for the use of public resources.
Prove that every public service must earn a commercial profit.
objectives.explanation: Budget comparison helps assess whether resources were used within authorised plans and explain variances.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: Which control best supports traceability in a computerised accounting system?
options: Allowing all users to edit approved records without a log.
Individual user accounts with permissions and logs of changes.
One shared administrator password for all staff.
Deleting every transaction history after posting.
objectives.explanation: Identifiable users and recorded changes help establish responsibility and investigate errors.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: Which practice most directly improves the verifiability of a recorded purchase?
options: Retain the invoice and evidence that the goods were received.
Record an amount solely because it seems plausible.
Destroy the supplier’s invoice after entering an estimate.
Change the date to whichever period gives the highest profit.
objectives.explanation: Supporting documents allow others to trace the entry to evidence of the transaction.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: Why is consistent use of an accounting policy helpful when comparing periods?
options: It means no policy may ever change for any reason.
It guarantees that the business becomes more profitable.
It makes supporting evidence unnecessary.
It reduces changes caused solely by switching methods, making trends easier to interpret.
objectives.explanation: Consistency supports comparability while justified and properly explained changes can still be appropriate.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: Which action best reflects prudent accounting rather than deliberate bias?
options: Recognise all hoped-for profits as already earned.
Omit known liabilities to make the business look stronger.
Use a supportable allowance for expected receivable losses.
Understate every asset regardless of evidence.
objectives.explanation: Prudence requires care under uncertainty, not arbitrary suppression of income or creation of hidden reserves.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: Electricity used in December will be paid for in January. In December’s accrual accounts it should normally be recorded as
options: nothing, solely because cash has not yet moved.
an expense and an accrued liability.
drawings and a cash receipt.
sales revenue and a non-current asset.
objectives.explanation: The expense belongs to the period of use even though payment follows later.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: A portion of insurance paid before year-end covers the next accounting period. The unused portion is normally
options: a prepayment reported as an asset.
a trade-sales return.
an extra current-period expense with no future benefit.
an overdraft created by a customer.
objectives.explanation: The payment secures a future benefit and is excluded from the current period’s insurance expense.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: Trade receivables are shown after deducting an allowance for doubtful amounts. The deduction principally represents
options: cash deposited in a separate customer account.
a guarantee that all customers will default.
additional sales made after year-end.
an estimate of amounts not expected to be collected.
objectives.explanation: It adjusts the reported recoverable amount without implying that cash has already been received.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: Inventory cost is ₦18,000 and estimated net realisable value is ₦15,000. Using the stated lower-of-cost-and-net-realisable-value rule, what carrying amount is used?
objectives.explanation: The stated rule selects the lower recoverable amount.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: Rent of a production workshop is normally classified in a manufacturing account as
options: a customer’s trade discount.
factory overhead.
selling commission only.
the proprietor’s drawings.
objectives.explanation: Workshop rent supports production generally and is not normally traceable to one individual unit as a direct material.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: A royalty is payable for every unit manufactured under a licence. If directly attributable to those units, it is classified as
options: a direct expense.
an unrelated office donation.
a purchase of share capital.
a loan received from customers.
objectives.explanation: The per-unit production charge can be traced to the output for which it is incurred.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: Subscriptions received in advance by a club relate to the next membership period. At year-end they are normally
options: current-period income solely because cash was received.
an irrecoverable trade debt.
a depreciation charge.
a liability until earned.
objectives.explanation: The club has received cash for a period whose service or membership entitlement is still to be provided.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: Which item can appear in a receipts and payments account but is not itself income in an income and expenditure account?
options: A donation earned and received for current activities.
Current-year interest income received.
Cash received from selling an old equipment asset.
Subscriptions earned and received for the current year.
objectives.explanation: Receipts and payments include capital cash flows; the full sale proceeds are not ordinary subscription income or a direct measure of gain.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: Two departments share a building. Which basis is most directly relevant for allocating building rent when their occupied areas differ?
options: The date each customer was born.
Floor area used by each department.
The first letter of each manager’s name.
A random number unrelated to use.
objectives.explanation: An allocation basis should reflect the cost’s relationship to departmental use; floor area is relevant to occupation cost.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: Goods sent to a branch are invoiced above cost for internal control. Before reporting group profit, why must internal loading on unsold branch goods be considered?
options: Internal mark-up is not profit earned from an external customer.
Every transfer creates a sale to an independent outside customer.
Internal mark-up is automatically additional cash in the bank.
The physical goods cease to be inventory at the branch.
objectives.explanation: Unrealised internal profit must not inflate the group’s inventory or profit in the stated basic model.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: Why is depreciation commonly added back to profit when calculating operating cash flow by an indirect reconciliation?
options: It is always cash received from customers.
It increases every trade payable directly.
It is the same as proceeds from selling the asset.
It reduced profit without itself being a cash payment in that period.
objectives.explanation: Adding back removes the non-cash expense’s effect in the profit-to-cash reconciliation; it does not create new cash.

objectives.subject: Financial Accounting
objectives.prompt: A purchases-ledger control account has a credit balance after all entries are reconciled. In the basic model without supplier advances, what does this balance represent?
options: The total amount owed to credit suppliers.
The selling value of closing inventory.
The total amount owed by credit customers.
The proprietor’s personal savings.
objectives.explanation: The control account summarises supplier balances. Its closing credit balance represents a payable, rather than goods held or customer debts.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: Residents obey a council mainly because they accept its right to make decisions, rather than because they fear punishment. Which concept is most directly illustrated?
options: Military power.
Population density.
Legitimacy.
Territorial size.
objectives.explanation: Legitimacy concerns acceptance of the right to rule; coercive capacity alone does not establish that acceptance.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: A cultural community shares language and historical identity but lives across several independent states. Which description best fits the community?
options: A political party by definition.
A nation that does not coincide with one state.
One necessarily sovereign state.
A local-government department.
objectives.explanation: A nation concerns shared identity; a state concerns political organisation, territory and sovereignty.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: An official is required to answer a charge through the same publicly established court procedure used for other citizens. Which principle is most directly supported?
options: Equality before the law.
Government by personal decree.
Hereditary succession.
Unrestricted executive discretion.
objectives.explanation: The scenario applies legal procedures to an official rather than granting arbitrary exemption from them.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: A legislative committee questions ministers about how approved public funds were spent. This is primarily an example of
options: judicial sentencing of ministers.
executive appointment of judges.
direct election of civil servants.
legislative oversight of the executive.
objectives.explanation: The committee checks executive performance without necessarily administering the programme itself.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: A constitution requires a special supermajority and additional approval to amend its principal provisions. It is described as rigid mainly because
options: it must be changed by the executive alone.
it can never be amended under any circumstances.
amendment is harder than passing ordinary legislation.
it cannot contain any written provisions.
objectives.explanation: Rigidity concerns the amendment procedure, not whether the document can ever be changed.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: In a federation, what most clearly distinguishes constituent governments’ constitutional powers from ordinary administrative delegation?
options: Every local official is elected by all citizens nationally.
The powers are constitutionally allocated and cannot simply be withdrawn as an ordinary administrative instruction.
The constituent governments necessarily have identical populations.
The central government has no powers of any kind.
objectives.explanation: Federal distribution is protected by the constitution; routine delegation depends more directly on the delegating authority.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: Which feature is most characteristic of a confederation in the conventional textbook distinction?
options: Member states retain sovereignty while assigning limited common responsibilities to joint institutions.
All member identities disappear into one unitary administration.
One hereditary ruler must control every member state.
Constituent units have no independent political existence.
objectives.explanation: A confederation is based on cooperation among sovereign members rather than necessarily creating a single sovereign federal state.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: Which feature most directly distinguishes a presidential executive from a parliamentary executive in the usual models?
options: A presidential system has no legislature.
A parliamentary system cannot hold elections.
A president must be a hereditary monarch.
The president normally holds a separately constituted mandate rather than remaining in office solely through legislative confidence.
objectives.explanation: A parliamentary executive depends on legislative confidence; the ordinary presidential model separates the executive mandate and tenure from that mechanism.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: Under collective cabinet responsibility, a minister who fundamentally rejects an agreed cabinet policy is normally expected to
options: dismiss the entire legislature personally.
transfer all executive powers to a court clerk.
support the common policy publicly or leave the cabinet.
remain in cabinet while treating every agreed decision as optional.
objectives.explanation: Collective responsibility requires a united public position while a minister remains part of the cabinet.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: Why might a legislature authorise a ministry to make detailed technical regulations under an enabling law?
options: The legislature ceases to exist after one delegation.
Technical detail can be handled within authority and limits set by the legislature.
Delegation makes the constitution irrelevant.
A ministry then gains unlimited power to change any law.
objectives.explanation: Delegated legislation can use expertise and flexibility while remaining subject to the enabling law and oversight.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: A permanent official implements lawful policy under successive elected governments without campaigning for one party in the office. This illustrates
options: political neutrality of the civil service.
automatic membership of the governing party.
judicial immunity for all administrative errors.
abolition of ministerial accountability.
objectives.explanation: Neutrality supports professional continuity while elected officeholders determine policy within lawful authority.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: What is a central distinction between a pressure group and a political party?
options: Every pressure group must contest all parliamentary seats.
Parties are forbidden to propose policies.
Pressure groups can represent only business owners.
A pressure group chiefly seeks to influence policy, while a party seeks to win and exercise governmental office.
objectives.explanation: Methods can overlap, but their primary institutional purposes differ.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: Under a hypothetical exact proportional allocation with no threshold, a party wins 24% of valid votes for 100 seats. How many seats would it receive?
objectives.explanation: The stated rule gives 0.24×100 = 24 seats. Actual systems may use thresholds or rounding rules, which are excluded here.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: In a single-member election using plurality, A wins 40 votes, B 35 and C 25. Which statement is correct?
options: C wins because C has the fewest votes.
A wins despite receiving less than half of the valid votes.
B wins because the two losing candidates together exceed A.
A must receive 51 votes before any plurality winner can be declared.
objectives.explanation: Plurality selects the largest vote total; it does not necessarily require an absolute majority.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: Which action most directly improves the accuracy of an electoral register without deliberately excluding eligible voters?
options: Provide a documented process to correct duplicate and erroneous entries with opportunities to challenge mistakes.
Delete all entries from areas where turnout was previously low.
Allow candidates to remove opponents’ supporters without evidence.
Treat every spelling error as permanent loss of voting rights.
objectives.explanation: Accuracy and fair correction protect register integrity while reducing wrongful exclusion.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: An electoral commission is legally described as independent but cannot obtain approved operational funds unless a candidate authorises each payment. What is the main concern?
options: Legal independence proves that financial arrangements can never matter.
Candidates must therefore become the judges of every complaint.
Operational funding has no connection with election administration.
Financial dependence can undermine practical independence.
objectives.explanation: Formal status alone does not remove opportunities for operational interference through funding.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: A website poll asks visitors whether they support a policy. Why should its result not automatically be treated as the opinion of all citizens?
options: All respondents must deliberately lie.
Public opinion can never be studied with any evidence.
Participants self-select and may differ from citizens who do not visit or respond.
The number of responses alone guarantees national representativeness.
objectives.explanation: A voluntary online sample can have coverage and selection bias.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: Naturalisation is best described generally as
options: membership of a trade association.
a legal process through which a non-citizen acquires citizenship after meeting the state’s requirements.
automatic citizenship from buying a local newspaper.
temporary permission to cross a border for one day.
objectives.explanation: The precise requirements vary; the concept is acquisition through the recognised legal process rather than citizenship arising automatically from any visit.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: A child gradually learns political attitudes through family discussion, schooling and media. This process is
options: political socialisation.
legislative dissolution.
territorial annexation.
judicial review.
objectives.explanation: Political socialisation develops political orientations through social experience and institutions.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: Which method is most characteristic of British indirect rule in its conventional colonial form?
options: Granting immediate equal sovereignty to every village.
Eliminating all local intermediaries in every region.
Holding universal adult elections for all colonial offices.
Governing through recognised local authorities under colonial supervision.
objectives.explanation: Indirect rule used existing or constructed local authority structures rather than relying solely on direct rule by European officials at every level.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: Why could indirect rule operate differently in a centralised emirate and a community governed through dispersed assemblies?
options: Geography alone determined every political institution.
Decentralised communities had no ways of making collective decisions.
The pre-existing distribution of authority affected which intermediaries could exercise accepted power.
All communities already had identical office structures.
objectives.explanation: A uniform colonial administrative label could encounter very different local institutions and legitimacy.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: Which feature is commonly associated with political organisation in many pre-colonial Igbo communities?
options: A single colonial governor before European colonial rule.
Decision-making involving village assemblies and several institutions rather than one uniform central monarch.
One identical absolute emperor ruling all communities.
The complete absence of collective decision-making.
objectives.explanation: Many communities had decentralised arrangements, though practices varied and should not be described as identical everywhere.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: Which constitutional development is associated with the Clifford Constitution of 1922 in Nigeria?
options: A limited elective principle for representation in Lagos and Calabar.
Universal adult suffrage throughout all regions.
Adoption of the 1979 presidential system.
Abolition of British colonial rule in 1922.
objectives.explanation: The reform introduced limited elected representation; it did not establish universal adult suffrage or national independence.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: How could the experiences of the Second World War strengthen anti-colonial nationalism in West Africa?
options: The war automatically granted independence to every colony on one date.
All nationalist organisations disappeared permanently.
Returning servicemen had no possible influence on political ideas.
Service, wider contact and demands for freedom could intensify criticism of colonial inequality.
objectives.explanation: Wartime experiences and international ideas could challenge colonial claims, without being the only cause of nationalism.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: In the historical idea of non-alignment, the main aim was to
options: promise automatic support for one bloc in every dispute.
abolish the sovereignty of participating states.
preserve independent foreign-policy judgement rather than automatically join a rival power bloc.
end all diplomatic relations with every state.
objectives.explanation: Non-alignment is not equivalent to refusing every international relationship or remaining neutral on every issue.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: An officer gives an instruction within powers attached to the office and recognised procedures. This illustrates authority mainly as
options: any personal preference expressed by a resident.
the recognised right to issue binding decisions within a defined role.
the physical size of a territory.
the total number of soldiers in a state.
objectives.explanation: Authority differs from the mere ability to compel compliance by force.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: External sovereignty refers mainly to a state’s
options: independence from another state’s supreme political control.
guaranteed economic self-sufficiency.
absence of every international agreement.
ability to ignore all physical geography.
objectives.explanation: External sovereignty concerns the state’s position in relation to other states, rather than the popularity of one government.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: A constitutional monarchy can coexist with parliamentary government when
options: the monarch must personally decide every court case.
there can be no elected legislature.
the constitution forbids all ministerial accountability.
the monarch’s role is constitutionally limited while ministers conduct government under the relevant parliamentary rules.
objectives.explanation: Monarchical headship does not necessarily mean unlimited personal rule.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: A central ministry posts its own officers to regional offices while retaining decision-making power. This is most clearly
options: a treaty-based confederation.
automatic constitutional devolution of autonomous power.
deconcentration.
the creation of sovereign independent states.
objectives.explanation: Administrative work is geographically dispersed without necessarily transferring autonomous powers to separate local governments.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: Which is a basic function of a constitution?
options: Guarantee that no political disagreement can arise.
Define institutions, their powers and the framework for governing.
Replace every government budget with one permanent figure.
List every private purchase made by all citizens.
objectives.explanation: A constitution establishes the governing framework rather than merely recording each day’s administrative tasks.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: Why can secure judicial tenure, subject to a proper removal process, support judicial independence?
options: It reduces pressure to decide cases merely to avoid arbitrary dismissal.
It makes every judicial decision correct automatically.
It removes all professional obligations from judges.
It makes the executive the final author of every judgment.
objectives.explanation: Security of tenure can protect impartial decision-making while appropriate accountability mechanisms remain possible.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: Several parties agree to form a government because none can command the required legislative support alone. This is a
options: military coup by definition.
hereditary succession.
single-party monopoly by definition.
coalition government.
objectives.explanation: A coalition combines parties to obtain or maintain the necessary governing support.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: A legislative quorum requirement primarily ensures that
options: only the speaker may attend proceedings.
all members must belong to one party.
a minimum number of members is present for specified business to proceed.
every bill must receive unanimous national approval.
objectives.explanation: Quorum concerns valid participation in proceedings, not the final vote share needed to pass every type of bill.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: An ombudsman-type institution investigates complaints about administrative unfairness. Its principal concern is
options: selecting candidates in every party primary.
maladministration and related grievances.
commanding the armed forces in wartime.
printing legal-tender currency.
objectives.explanation: The role is administrative complaint investigation, distinct from replacing every ordinary court or conducting all elections.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: A party primary is mainly used to
options: select the party’s candidate for an election.
amend every clause of the national constitution.
appoint all civil servants permanently.
settle every electoral petition in court.
objectives.explanation: Internal nomination differs from the general electorate choosing an officeholder.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: Citizens vote directly on a specified public question rather than choosing representatives. This is a
options: cabinet reshuffle.
judicial appeal.
legislative adjournment.
referendum.
objectives.explanation: A referendum asks electors to decide an issue directly.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: A government claims that an emergency allows any official to detain any critic indefinitely without review. Which concern is strongest from a constitutionalist perspective?
options: Every criticism of government is automatically a criminal offence.
Declaring an emergency permanently abolishes the constitution.
Emergency powers still need defined legal limits and safeguards against arbitrary use.
Public officials should have no legal powers in any emergency.
objectives.explanation: Constitutionalism examines how power is constrained and reviewed, rather than treating an emergency label as unlimited authority.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: Which activity demonstrates lawful political participation between elections?
options: Destroying public records to hide a complaint.
Submitting evidence and a petition to a public hearing.
Falsifying another citizen’s registration details.
Threatening witnesses to prevent a hearing.
objectives.explanation: Participation includes organised communication and scrutiny beyond casting a ballot.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: Publishing a spending total without records of approvals, recipients or delivered work gives weak accountability because
options: the public cannot readily trace the total to authorised transactions and outcomes.
a single total necessarily proves that every payment was stolen.
supporting records have no relevance once a total is announced.
public spending can never be documented.
objectives.explanation: Accountability requires evidence that allows spending and responsibility to be checked.

objectives.subject: Government
objectives.prompt: Two neighbouring states resolve a boundary disagreement through negotiation and mediation. These methods primarily illustrate
options: automatic territorial conquest.
abolition of both governments.
a compulsory merger of all neighbouring states.
peaceful diplomatic dispute management.
objectives.explanation: Negotiation and mediation seek an agreed settlement through dialogue rather than force.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: On a map at 1:25,000, a rectangular field measures 2 cm by 3 cm. What is its ground area?
options: 0.06 km²
1.25 km²
3.75 km²
objectives.explanation: The ground dimensions are 0.5 km and 0.75 km, so area = 0.5×0.75 = 0.375 km².

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: A whole-circle bearing of 135° points generally towards the
options: north-east.
south-west.
north-west.
south-east.
objectives.explanation: Bearings are measured clockwise from north; 135° lies halfway between east and south.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Contours cross a stream in V-shapes whose tips point west. With no other complications, the stream most likely flows towards the
options: north along every contour.
south along every contour.
east.
west.
objectives.explanation: Contour Vs in a valley usually point upstream, so downstream is away from their tips.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Why are eastings read before northings when stating a conventional grid reference?
options: Both numbers refer only to magnetic north.
The reference locates the horizontal position first and then the vertical position.
Eastings give height and northings give rainfall.
Northings always measure distance from a coastline.
objectives.explanation: The ordering convention distinguishes coordinates and avoids interchanging positions; it is not a measure of elevation.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Ignoring time zones and daylight-saving rules, what is local solar time at 75°E when it is 08:00 at Greenwich?
objectives.explanation: At 15° per hour, 75° east is five solar hours ahead: 08:00+5 hours = 13:00.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: What chiefly explains the annual change in the angle of sunlight and day length at a fixed mid-latitude location?
options: A daily reversal of Earth’s rotation.
The Moon blocking sunlight every afternoon.
Earth’s axis becoming vertical each month.
Earth’s axial tilt combined with its revolution around the Sun.
objectives.explanation: The tilted axis changes seasonal solar geometry as Earth orbits; daily rotation alone explains the day-night cycle rather than the annual pattern.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Which setting is most strongly associated with an oceanic plate descending beneath another plate?
options: A transform boundary with only horizontal sliding.
A stable continental interior with no plate interaction.
A convergent boundary with subduction.
A divergent boundary creating only new oceanic crust.
objectives.explanation: Subduction occurs as plates converge and one descends, rather than simply moving apart.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Rainwater containing weak carbonic acid dissolves limestone. This is primarily
options: wind abrasion.
chemical weathering by carbonation.
freeze-thaw action.
exfoliation caused only by heating.
objectives.explanation: The rock’s material changes or dissolves through chemical reaction, unlike purely mechanical breakdown.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Why can prolonged rainfall increase the likelihood of a landslide on a steep, unstable slope?
options: Added water can increase mass and reduce the material’s resistance to movement.
Rainfall always removes gravity from the slope.
Water necessarily makes every slope permanently stronger.
All slope material becomes solid bedrock immediately.
objectives.explanation: Saturation and pore-water effects can destabilise slope material; rainfall does not guarantee failure on every slope.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: A river enters a lake and loses velocity. Which process is most likely near the entry point?
options: Uniform acceleration of all sediment upstream.
Creation of new sediment by plate subduction in the channel.
Immediate evaporation of the entire lake.
Deposition of some transported sediment.
objectives.explanation: Lower flow energy reduces the river’s capacity to carry part of its sediment load.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: An oxbow lake most directly forms when
options: a river is forced to flow uphill indefinitely.
groundwater dissolves a complete volcanic cone.
a meander loop is cut off from the main river channel.
a glacier deepens every desert basin.
objectives.explanation: A new shorter channel can isolate the old meander, leaving a curved water body.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: What produces the zigzag movement of beach sediment during longshore drift?
options: Tides prevent all sediment movement.
Oblique swash carries material up the beach, while backwash returns it more directly down the slope.
Both swash and backwash always travel exactly parallel to the coast.
Only vertical tectonic uplift moves every grain.
objectives.explanation: The combination yields a net movement along the shore when waves approach obliquely.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Which drainage feature is commonly associated with permeable, jointed limestone terrain?
options: Streams may disappear into sinkholes and flow underground.
All rainfall must remain on the surface.
Every valley necessarily contains a permanent surface river.
Limestone cannot be affected by water.
objectives.explanation: Water can enter joints and solution openings, supporting underground drainage.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Moist air rises over a mountain, cools and produces rain on the windward slope. The rain is mainly
options: rain caused only by a passing warm front.
rain formed without cooling or uplift.
a measurement of atmospheric pressure.
orographic rainfall.
objectives.explanation: Relief forces moist air upwards; a leeward rain shadow may develop.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Which instrument is designed to collect precipitation for measurement of rainfall depth?
options: Wind vane.
Hygrometer.
Rain gauge.
Anemometer.
objectives.explanation: A rain gauge collects rainfall over a known opening so the depth can be measured.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Air cools to its dew point without first losing water vapour. What is likely to begin if suitable condensation surfaces or nuclei are available?
options: A reversal of Earth’s rotation.
Condensation as the air becomes saturated.
An automatic increase in the saturation capacity of the cooler air.
Complete destruction of all atmospheric moisture.
objectives.explanation: Cooling reduces the amount of water vapour required for saturation, so condensation can begin at the dew point.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Which annual pattern is most consistent with a humid equatorial climate?
options: High temperatures and substantial rainfall in most months.
Very low temperatures throughout the year.
Rainfall only as winter snow.
No rainfall for several consecutive years as the defining norm.
objectives.explanation: Humid equatorial climates generally lack the long dry season characteristic of many tropical continental climates.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Strong leaching under hot, wet conditions can leave tropical soils enriched in relatively less soluble iron compounds. This is associated with
options: the complete absence of chemical weathering.
permanent freezing of soil water.
accumulation of unaltered sea salt as the only soil process.
lateritic soil development.
objectives.explanation: Intense weathering and removal of soluble material can concentrate iron and aluminium compounds.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Large buttress roots in some tropical rainforest trees mainly help
options: replace all leaves in photosynthesis.
prevent the tree from taking up any water.
support tall trees in relatively shallow rooting conditions.
make every root an aquatic breathing tube.
objectives.explanation: Wide supports can stabilise the trunk; not every rainforest species has identical root structures.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: A hypothetical district has 200,000 people in 4,000 km². What is its arithmetic population density?
options: 800 people per km²
50 people per km²
0.02 people per km²
500 people per km²
objectives.explanation: Density = population/area = 200,000/4,000 = 50 people per km².

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: An area has a birth rate of 42 per thousand and a death rate of 18 per thousand. Ignoring migration, its annual rate of natural increase is
objectives.explanation: Natural increase is 24 per thousand, equal to 24/10 = 2.4%.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Houses develop in a narrow line along a major road. The settlement pattern is best described as
options: radial around one central point only.
randomly dispersed with no corridor.
concentric circular rings by definition.
linear.
objectives.explanation: A transport route can guide development along an elongated corridor.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: A cement plant is placed near a major limestone quarry. Which locational consideration most directly explains this choice?
options: Avoiding every connection with a market.
Maximising the distance from all raw materials.
Reducing the movement cost of a bulky major raw material.
Ensuring that no electricity is needed.
objectives.explanation: Cement uses substantial limestone input, so proximity can reduce raw-material transport costs.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: A GIS stores roads as connected lines and settlements as points. These are examples of
options: an instrument for measuring humidity.
vector data.
raster pixels only.
a single non-spatial text paragraph.
objectives.explanation: Vector representations use points, lines and polygons, unlike a raster grid of cells.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: A town replaces vegetated ground with roofs and paved roads without improving drainage. During similar heavy rainfall, a likely result is
options: more rapid surface runoff and increased local flood pressure.
all rainfall infiltrates faster because of the paving.
river discharge must become zero.
the amount of rain falling is automatically halved.
objectives.explanation: Impermeable surfaces reduce infiltration and can deliver water to drains more quickly.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Which statement correctly compares maps at 1:25,000 and 1:100,000?
options: The 1:100,000 map is the larger-scale map.
Both show exactly the same ground distance per centimetre.
The denominator does not affect represented ground area.
The 1:25,000 map shows a smaller ground area on the same paper size but can show more detail.
objectives.explanation: A larger map scale represents less ground per unit of map length.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: A spot height on a topographic map gives
options: the compass bearing of the nearest road.
the population of a whole grid square.
the elevation of a specific point relative to the stated datum.
the average monthly rainfall at every point on a contour.
objectives.explanation: A spot height applies to a point, whereas a contour joins locations of equal elevation.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: A wind described as north-easterly blows mainly
options: from the north-west towards the south-east.
from the north-east towards the south-west.
from the south-west towards the north-east.
only vertically downwards.
objectives.explanation: Wind names normally indicate the direction from which the wind comes.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Intense surface heating causes moist air to rise, cool and form rain clouds. This rainfall mechanism is
options: convectional.
orographic solely because a mountain blocks the air.
a groundwater-flow process.
an effect requiring permanent snow cover.
objectives.explanation: Heating at the surface initiates uplift, unlike uplift forced mainly by a mountain or frontal boundary.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Compared with an otherwise similar coast influenced by a cold current, a warm current can
options: remove every seasonal change everywhere.
turn all seawater into freshwater.
prevent any moisture exchange between sea and air.
raise coastal temperatures by transferring heat from warmer water to the air.
objectives.explanation: Ocean currents can influence nearby air temperature, though winds and other factors also matter.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: A roughly cone-shaped volcanic mountain has streams flowing outward in many directions from its high centre. The drainage pattern is
options: centripetal towards one central low basin.
rectangular solely because streams turn at right angles.
radial.
trellis along alternating parallel rock bands.
objectives.explanation: Streams diverge down the slopes from a central high point.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Which observation most strongly supports identifying a rock as sedimentary?
options: A wholly molten sample at the surface.
Distinct bedding containing preserved fossils.
Fresh glassy texture with gas bubbles from lava.
Large interlocking crystals without layers.
objectives.explanation: Bedding and fossils are characteristic evidence for many sedimentary rocks, unlike a purely interlocking crystalline texture.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Groundwater is pumped out of an aquifer faster than long-term recharge replaces it. What is a likely consequence?
options: A declining water table and reduced groundwater availability.
The aquifer gains unlimited new water automatically.
Recharge becomes irrelevant because storage is always infinite.
All wells must rise at exactly the same rate.
objectives.explanation: Persistent withdrawal above recharge depletes stored groundwater, although local conditions affect the rate.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: On a cultivated slope, contour ploughing can reduce soil erosion because the furrows
options: guide all water straight down the steepest path.
remove every soil particle immediately.
prevent any rainfall from reaching the field.
interrupt downslope flow and slow surface runoff.
objectives.explanation: Following contours can retain or slow water, unlike furrows running directly downhill.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Which distinction between renewable and non-renewable resources is most accurate?
options: Fossil fuels are replenished as quickly as they are burned.
Non-renewable resources have no economic uses.
Renewable resources can be replenished on relevant human timescales, but use can still exceed renewal.
Every renewable resource is impossible to deplete.
objectives.explanation: Renewability does not mean an unlimited supply under any level of extraction.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: A population pyramid with a very broad base most directly indicates
options: an exact income level for every household.
a large proportion of young people.
that every adult has emigrated.
a population consisting mainly of elderly people.
objectives.explanation: The lower age groups form the base; the shape alone does not give a precise future population total.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Why can a tourism-dependent town experience seasonal employment?
options: Visitor demand may rise and fall during particular parts of the year.
All tourism workers must move abroad monthly.
Tourism demand is necessarily identical every day.
Seasonal employment can occur only in mining.
objectives.explanation: Businesses can adjust staffing to seasonal flows, although some employment may remain throughout the year.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: In a hot irrigated area with poor drainage, repeated evaporation can contribute to
options: the guaranteed removal of every salt from the root zone.
permanent freezing of the field.
a complete stop to groundwater movement worldwide.
salt accumulation in the upper soil.
objectives.explanation: Water is lost while dissolved salts can remain, especially where drainage and leaching are inadequate.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: A low-lying delta crossed by distributaries and wetlands is likely to face which settlement constraint?
options: The complete absence of surface water.
Permanent polar ice cover.
Flood risk and waterlogged ground in some locations.
Universal steep mountain slopes.
objectives.explanation: Low relief, channels and wet ground can complicate building and transport; local conditions vary.

objectives.subject: Geography
objectives.prompt: Abandoned surface-mining ground has exposed loose material and developing gullies. Which restoration action most directly addresses erosion?
options: Dump more loose spoil on unstable slopes without drainage.
Stabilise slopes and establish suitable vegetation while managing runoff.
Concentrate all runoff into unprotected steep channels.
Remove every remaining plant cover.
objectives.explanation: Reducing exposed unstable surfaces and controlling concentrated flow can limit further soil loss.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Which enterprise is most directly part of horticulture?
options: Rearing cattle for beef.
