Producing vegetables and ornamental flowers.
Managing timber trees for sawn wood.
Raising fish in ponds.
objectives.explanation: Horticulture includes the cultivation of vegetables, fruits and ornamental plants.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Which pairing correctly links an agricultural raw material with an agro-allied industry?
options: Cotton and textile manufacture.
Cocoa and hide tanning.
Maize and latex processing.
Sugarcane and sawmilling.
objectives.explanation: Cotton fibre is an important textile input.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: A farmer grows maize and beans together on the same plot during the same season. This is
options: crop rotation only.
mixed farming solely because two crops are present.
monocropping.
mixed cropping.
objectives.explanation: Mixed cropping involves more than one crop on a plot at the same time; it is not necessarily mixed farming, which includes livestock.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Integrating suitable trees with crops or livestock on agricultural land is generally called
options: Sole livestock production with no tree component.
A fish-hatchery system only.
agroforestry.
Crop rotation without any woody plant component.
objectives.explanation: Agroforestry combines woody plants with other farm components in a managed system.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Two uncompacted soils have similar organic content. One has much larger particles and pores. Which tendency is most likely?
options: Particle size cannot influence drainage.
Faster drainage and lower water retention in the coarser soil.
No water can ever enter the coarser soil.
The coarser soil must hold more water under every condition.
objectives.explanation: Large pores often permit rapid drainage, while fine pores can retain more water under comparable conditions.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Which distinction between soil texture and soil structure is correct?
options: Texture concerns proportions of particle sizes; structure concerns how particles are arranged into aggregates.
Texture concerns aggregate arrangement; structure concerns particle-size proportions.
Texture concerns only organic matter; structure concerns only soil pH.
Texture and structure both mean only the colour of the topsoil.
objectives.explanation: The two describe different physical characteristics and should not be treated as interchangeable.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Repeated heavy machinery traffic on wet soil can reduce crop performance mainly by
options: Increasing large pores and making root penetration easier.
Improving aeration by reducing soil bulk density.
Eliminating resistance to root growth in the compacted layer.
compacting pores and restricting aeration and root movement.
objectives.explanation: Compaction can reduce suitable pore space, infiltration and root penetration.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: In a well-functioning legume root nodule, nitrogen-fixing bacteria help the plant mainly by
options: supplying sunlight from the soil.
eliminating the need for every other nutrient.
converting atmospheric nitrogen into compounds that can enter biological use.
turning all soil water into carbon dioxide.
objectives.explanation: The association supplies biologically usable nitrogen; it is not direct manufacture of phosphorus.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: A soil test confirms excessive acidity for the intended crop. An appropriately selected liming treatment is used chiefly to
options: Lower the soil pH further.
reduce acidity and improve the soil reaction for that crop.
Supply every required nutrient in full without another assessment.
Remove salinity regardless of soil conditions.
objectives.explanation: Liming can raise pH under appropriate conditions; it is not a universal cure for every soil problem.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: A suitable mulch can conserve moisture chiefly by
options: reducing direct evaporation and moderating the exposed soil surface.
increasing direct sunlight on every soil particle.
making plant roots unnecessary.
stopping all rainfall infiltration.
objectives.explanation: Cover changes surface conditions; it does not add a guaranteed fixed amount of water.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Why should transplanted seedlings be handled to minimise root injury?
options: Root injury always makes every seedling grow faster.
Roots have no role until the plant flowers.
All transplanted seedlings must lose every root.
Damaged roots can reduce water uptake while the seedling establishes.
objectives.explanation: Root protection helps reduce transplant stress and supports water supply to the shoot.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Which planting material is commonly used to establish cassava vegetatively?
options: Detached storage-root pieces with no viable buds.
Mature leaf blades without stem sections.
Healthy stem cuttings.
Dried inflorescence fragments without viable propagules.
objectives.explanation: Cassava is commonly propagated from suitable stem sections with viable buds.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: A hypothetical one-hectare field is planted at 1 m between rows and 0.5 m within rows, one stand per position. Ignoring borders and paths, how many stands fit?

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: A traceable seed lot with reliable varietal-purity and germination information is useful because it
options: provides evidence about planting material quality before sowing.
guarantees that no field management is needed.
makes all varieties genetically identical.
replaces every requirement for suitable soil and water.
objectives.explanation: Quality information reduces uncertainty but does not guarantee success under every field condition.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Why is grain usually dried to a suitable storage moisture level before sealed storage?
options: Water content has no effect on stored grain.
Sealing automatically kills every mould under all conditions.
Drying converts all starch to protein.
Excess moisture can promote deterioration, heating and mould growth.
objectives.explanation: Appropriate drying and storage conditions help preserve quality; sealing wet grain does not make moisture harmless.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: A whitefly carries a virus from an infected cassava plant to another plant. In this relationship the whitefly is
options: a soil nutrient.
a variety of cassava root.
a vector.
the virus itself.
objectives.explanation: A vector transmits the pathogen; it is not necessarily the pathogen itself.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Why might a farmer conserve ladybirds that feed on aphids?
options: Predators always increase aphid reproduction.
They can act as natural enemies that reduce pest numbers.
Every insect on a farm is necessarily a crop pest.
Ladybirds replace all crop nutrients.
objectives.explanation: Beneficial predators can contribute to biological control within an integrated approach.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: How can adult ruminants obtain nutrients from fibrous feed that many non-ruminants use less efficiently?
options: Microorganisms in the rumen help break down cellulose.
The animal secretes cellulase from its teeth.
Fibrous particles are absorbed unchanged through the rumen wall.
Pepsin in the abomasum directly breaks down all cellulose.
objectives.explanation: Symbiotic microbes assist fermentation of fibrous material.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: In a brooder with other conditions suitable, chicks cluster tightly beneath the heat source. This pattern most strongly suggests that
options: Excessive heat causing avoidance of the heated centre.
Uniformly suitable warmth indicated by an even distribution.
A feed-conversion calculation rather than a temperature response.
the chicks may be too cold.
objectives.explanation: Clustering near heat is a standard behavioural indication of inadequate warmth, but observations should be assessed with other conditions.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Which farm record is most directly needed to track the number of bags entering and leaving a grain store?
options: A breeding history record only.
A cash book with no stock quantities.
A stock or inventory record.
A weather-observation record only.
objectives.explanation: Quantity movements identify receipts, issues and remaining stock; a list of staff birthdays does not.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: An extension officer demonstrates a new planting method on a small comparison plot with farmers. What is a major advantage?
options: It proves that one unreplicated observation is universal.
Farmers can observe results and ask questions before deciding on wider adoption.
It removes the need to consider local conditions.
It makes farmers legally unable to reject any advice.
objectives.explanation: A local demonstration can connect advice to evidence without guaranteeing identical results everywhere.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Why can dissolved oxygen in a productive pond be lowest near dawn?
options: Organisms respire overnight while photosynthesis is absent in darkness.
Photosynthesis is always fastest at midnight.
Fish do not respire during daylight.
Water can contain oxygen only when no algae are present.
objectives.explanation: Night-time respiration consumes oxygen without the daytime photosynthetic input.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Keeping bees can benefit nearby insect-pollinated crops mainly through
options: Fixing atmospheric nitrogen in crop root nodules.
Supplying mineral nutrients directly to crop roots.
Replacing every other pollination agent in all crops.
transfer of pollen while bees forage.
objectives.explanation: Pollination can support fertilisation and fruit or seed formation where the crop relies on insect visitors.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Which cost is most likely to vary with the number of broilers produced over a production cycle?
options: Depreciation on the existing shed for the same time period.
Land rent fixed for the production cycle.
Feed consumed by the birds.
An insurance premium fixed for the cycle.
objectives.explanation: Feed use generally changes with the number and growth of birds, unlike some short-run fixed facility costs.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Farm gross margin is conventionally calculated as
options: Total revenue minus fixed cost only.
total revenue minus total variable cost.
Total revenue minus all variable and fixed costs.
Total variable cost minus total revenue.
objectives.explanation: Gross margin excludes fixed costs; net profit requires further relevant deductions.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Which tool is designed for making controlled pruning cuts on suitable small branches?
options: Secateurs.
A garden rake.
A dibber.
A watering can.
objectives.explanation: Secateurs provide a cutting action appropriate for pruning within their intended capacity.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Why should an exposed rotating power shaft on farm machinery have its proper guard fitted?
options: It increases the shaft’s nutritional value.
It makes all maintenance unnecessary.
It guarantees that touching a moving shaft is safe.
It reduces the risk of clothing or body parts becoming entangled.
objectives.explanation: The guard is a protective barrier; servicing still requires safe isolation and competent procedures.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: A crop’s roots remain waterlogged for a prolonged period. What important function can be restricted?
options: The conversion of leaf chlorophyll directly into soil nitrogen.
An automatic increase in root-zone oxygen supply.
Aerobic root respiration because gas exchange is limited.
Complete replacement of root respiration by leaf transpiration.
objectives.explanation: Waterlogged pores contain less available air, which can constrain oxygen supply to roots.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: In grafting, the rootstock primarily supplies
options: The desired shoot attached above the graft union.
the root system onto which the scion is joined.
Only the pollen source for every fruit.
The root-free shoot tip before grafting.
objectives.explanation: The scion supplies the desired shoot portion, while the stock provides the rooted base.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: What is the main purpose of hardening nursery seedlings before field planting?
options: Gradually prepare them for less protected field conditions.
Make the stems completely dry and lifeless.
Stop the seedlings from ever using water.
Convert annual crops into perennial trees.
objectives.explanation: Controlled gradual exposure can improve adjustment rather than abruptly removing all protection.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Which description defines an annual crop?
options: It must need two growing seasons before completing its life cycle.
It necessarily remains productive for many years without completing its cycle.
It is defined by being planted in a dry rather than a wet season.
It normally completes its life cycle within one growing season or year.
objectives.explanation: Annual classification concerns the life cycle rather than the number of harvest workers.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: A viable seed has a coat that prevents sufficient water entry. This can cause
options: A guaranteed loss of viability in every embryo.
Successful germination regardless of water entry.
physical dormancy.
Vegetative propagation from the seed coat.
objectives.explanation: A water-impermeable coat can prevent germination despite viability and otherwise suitable conditions.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Weeds growing densely among young crops can reduce yield mainly by
options: preventing all insects from entering the farm.
competing for resources such as light, water and nutrients.
supplying unlimited extra light to every crop leaf.
making roots unnecessary.
objectives.explanation: Competition can limit crop access to essential resources.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Why should breeding decisions use performance records from animals managed under comparable conditions?
options: It helps separate inherited potential from differences caused by feeding or management.
A single appearance always reveals every inherited trait.
Nutrition has no possible effect on growth.
Records automatically eliminate all genetic variation.
objectives.explanation: Observed performance can reflect both genotype and environment.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: A balanced ration is one that
options: contains equal masses of every known feed ingredient.
contains only the cheapest ingredient regardless of nutrients.
is identical for a young chick and an adult cow.
supplies required nutrients in suitable amounts and proportions for the animal’s type and stage.
objectives.explanation: Requirements vary with species, age and production purpose; bulk alone does not define balance.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Which is an external parasite of livestock?
options: A tapeworm in the intestine.
A liver fluke inside the host.
A tick attached to the skin.
A roundworm in the digestive tract.
objectives.explanation: A tick lives on the external body surface, unlike an intestinal worm.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Why should milk containers be cleaned appropriately before use?
options: To remove all protein from the milk.
To reduce contamination of the collected milk.
To increase the number of disease-causing organisms.
To guarantee milk remains fresh indefinitely without suitable storage.
objectives.explanation: Clean equipment helps prevent introduction of unwanted microorganisms and residues; appearance alone does not establish hygiene.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: A pond is stocked far beyond its available oxygen and feeding capacity. What is a likely management problem?
options: Competition and poor water conditions can reduce growth and survival.
All fish must grow faster because crowding creates food.
Oxygen demand necessarily falls to zero.
The pond’s carrying capacity becomes unlimited.
objectives.explanation: More fish do not guarantee more harvest if supporting resources become limiting.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: Farm P harvests 6 tonnes from 3 hectares; farm Q harvests 5 tonnes from 2 hectares. Which has higher yield per hectare?
options: Farm P because its total output is larger.
Both because area cannot affect the calculation.
Neither because tonnes cannot be compared.
Farm Q.
objectives.explanation: P yields 2 t ha⁻¹, while Q yields 2.5 t ha⁻¹. Total output and output per area are different measures.

objectives.subject: Agricultural Science
objectives.prompt: A hypothetical land lease ends after two years, but a planned orchard will first produce after five years. What concern follows from these facts alone?
options: A lease date has no relevance to a long-term crop.
Planting trees automatically changes the written lease term.
The farmer may lose access before receiving the expected first harvest.
The orchard must mature within two months.
objectives.explanation: The stated tenure period and investment timeline do not match; no general legal rights beyond the scenario are assumed.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: Which component technology is most associated with second-generation computers in the conventional historical classification?
options: Vacuum tubes.
Integrated circuits as the defining second-generation replacement.
Microprocessors as the defining second-generation component.
Transistors.
objectives.explanation: The standard historical distinction associates second-generation machines with transistors replacing vacuum tubes.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: A user edits a document in ordinary working RAM but has not saved it when power fails. Why can the latest changes be lost?
options: The display is the permanent storage for all edits.
Power loss converts the document into firmware.
Working RAM is normally volatile and the unsaved changes may not be on persistent storage.
Every saved file is automatically deleted whenever RAM is used.
objectives.explanation: Saved files and temporary working contents are different; ordinary RAM does not preserve its contents through power loss.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: Firmware stored in non-volatile memory is useful during startup because
options: it must be erased every time power is removed.
it can provide initial instructions before the main operating system is loaded.
it is identical to every user’s unsaved spreadsheet.
it replaces all processors with a keyboard.
objectives.explanation: Startup requires instructions available without relying on an already running main operating system.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: Which CPU component is chiefly associated with arithmetic operations and logical comparisons?
options: Arithmetic and logic unit.
Control unit.
Memory address register.
Instruction register.
objectives.explanation: The ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations, while other components coordinate or store instructions and data.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: What is the greatest unsigned integer representable using 8 bits?
objectives.explanation: Eight bits provide 2⁸ patterns representing 0 through 2⁸−1.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: A field uses exactly 64 bits. How many bytes is this, using 8 bits per byte?
options: 64 bytes
512 bytes
8 bytes
4 bytes
objectives.explanation: 64/8 = 8 bytes. The question concerns storage units rather than text encoding assumptions.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: For a two-input AND gate, what is the output when the inputs are 1 and 0?
options: An undefined third truth value.
objectives.explanation: AND outputs 1 only when both inputs are 1.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: A NOT gate receives input 0. Its output is
options: The unchanged pair 00.
objectives.explanation: NOT reverses a binary truth value.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: An assembler primarily translates
options: Machine-code instructions back into high-level source code.
Spreadsheet formulas directly into paper layout settings.
A complete high-level program as its defining source language.
assembly-language instructions into machine-code representation.
objectives.explanation: An assembler operates on assembly language rather than serving as a word processor or database form.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: Which task is normally part of an operating system’s role?
options: Replace every hardware component physically.
Determine the truth of every web page.
Manage memory and coordinate running processes.
Write every student’s essay automatically as its defining function.
objectives.explanation: The operating system manages resources and provides services to applications.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: A spreadsheet formula =B2*C2 is copied one row down using ordinary relative references. What does the copied formula become?
objectives.explanation: Both row references move down by one while the columns remain the same.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: Which reference keeps both its row and column fixed when a spreadsheet formula is copied?
options: F1
objectives.explanation: Dollar signs before both column and row make both components absolute in the stated common spreadsheet notation.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: Why is a unique student admission number a suitable primary key for a student table?
options: It must contain the student’s complete address.
It guarantees that every other field is correct.
It is needed only for choosing font colour.
It can identify each student record without relying on names being unique.
objectives.explanation: A key distinguishes records; two students can legitimately have the same name.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: Which database operation most directly returns records whose class field equals “SS1”?
options: A data-entry form used only to add new rows.
A report-layout change with no selection criteria.
A query with the appropriate selection condition.
An import of every record without filtering.
objectives.explanation: A selection query filters records according to criteria.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: A school connects computers within its own nearby buildings for shared services. This is most naturally described as
options: a storage file extension.
a local area network.
the entire World Wide Web by definition.
an international satellite system only.
objectives.explanation: LAN describes a local network scope rather than a guarantee about public internet access.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: What is the main role of a router in an ordinary IP network?
options: Forward packets between networks according to routing information.
Forward frames only within a local segment using MAC addresses as its defining role.
Resolve hostnames as its defining routing operation.
Allocate spreadsheet cell formats to network addresses.
objectives.explanation: A router connects network paths; it is distinct from a document editor or a passive cable.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: A browser knows a website’s hostname but needs an IP address for a connection. Which service commonly supplies the name-to-address information?
options: A word-processing spelling checker.
A printer’s paper sensor.
A spreadsheet’s sorting tool.
DNS.
objectives.explanation: The Domain Name System supports hostname resolution; it does not itself prove that a site’s content is trustworthy.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: What does HTTPS primarily add to an ordinary web connection?
options: A guarantee that the site operator cannot deceive users.
A guarantee that the server and user device are free of malware.
Protection of the connection through TLS, rather than a guarantee that the site’s claims are truthful.
Automatic backup of every file on the user device.
objectives.explanation: Encryption and authentication of the connection are different from verifying every statement or offer on the site.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: When sending one email to several unrelated recipients, which field can hide their addresses from one another in the ordinary recipient display?
options: Visible To addresses for every recipient.
Bcc.
Subject.
Cc.
objectives.explanation: Bcc conceals those recipients from the ordinary visible recipient list, though the sender and service still process the addresses.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: Trace this pseudocode: total←0; FOR k←1 TO 4 inclusive: total←total+k; END FOR; OUTPUT total. What is output?
objectives.explanation: The additions are 1+2+3+4 = 10.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: A field must contain an integer from 0 to 100 inclusive. Which input should a range-and-type validation reject?
objectives.explanation: 105 is outside the stated range; the other listed integers satisfy it.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: Why should a program be tested with values exactly at accepted limits as well as ordinary values?
options: Ordinary tests can never be useful.
Only the final screen colour determines correctness.
Boundary mistakes can remain hidden when only middle values are tested.
Boundary inputs automatically prove every internal algorithm is correct.
objectives.explanation: Testing endpoints helps detect incorrect comparisons such as < where ≤ is required.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: A user renames a text file from .txt to .jpg without converting its contents. What follows?
options: The file is automatically decoded and rewritten into JPEG pixel data.
The name changes, but the contents do not automatically become a valid JPEG image.
All image programs must accept the renamed content as a valid JPEG.
Renaming alone cryptographically authenticates the file contents.
objectives.explanation: A filename extension can indicate intended type, but renaming alone is not content conversion.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: Why is a successful restore test important for a backup plan?
options: It provides evidence that required data can actually be recovered in a usable form.
It guarantees there can never be a future device failure.
It means no further backups will ever be needed.
It replaces every need to identify which data was backed up.
objectives.explanation: A copied file or success message alone does not establish that recovery will work when needed.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: An AI system produces a confident reference to a book that cannot be found in reliable catalogues. What is the most appropriate conclusion?
options: Confidence proves the reference is authentic.
Every AI output is necessarily false.
The user should invent a publisher to complete the citation.
The reference needs verification; confident wording is not evidence that it exists.
objectives.explanation: Generated language can contain fabricated or mistaken details, so source checking remains necessary.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: Which description distinguishes an analogue representation from a digital one?
options: An analogue representation is defined by having only binary values.
Digital representations cannot describe measured physical quantities.
An analogue representation varies continuously, while a digital representation uses discrete values.
Analogue and digital refer only to the physical size of the equipment.
objectives.explanation: This distinguishes representations, not a claim that all physical devices are purely one kind at every stage.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: A touchscreen is an example of a device that can
options: perform no input function.
provide visual output and receive touch input.
only print hard-copy pages.
only store backups with no input or output.
objectives.explanation: The display and sensing functions support both directions of interaction.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: Why can a CPU cache improve performance?
options: It can provide faster access to frequently or recently needed data and instructions.
Store all user files permanently after power is removed.
Replace the processor control unit.
Increase installed physical RAM capacity without adding memory.
objectives.explanation: A cache reduces some slower memory accesses but does not eliminate the need for main memory or storage.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: An indexed image format allocates 4 bits to each pixel’s colour index. What is the maximum number of distinct indices?
objectives.explanation: Four bits encode 2⁴ = 16 different index values.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: A registration table requires each enrolment’s student number to match an existing student record. This rule mainly supports
options: automatic correctness of every student’s name.
deletion of all student identifiers.
referential integrity.
a larger font size.
objectives.explanation: The reference must point to a valid related record rather than create an enrolment for a non-existent student.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: A cell stores the numeric value 0.25 and is displayed using percentage formatting with no decimal places. What is normally displayed?
options: The word quarter in every spreadsheet.
objectives.explanation: Percentage formatting displays the stored fraction as a percentage without changing its underlying value to 25.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: In a sequential file organisation, records are typically processed
options: in an ordered sequence rather than accessed solely by a direct location calculation.
Only by a hash calculation that jumps directly to each record.
Only through a network protocol with no records.
Only by changing the file extension before every read.
objectives.explanation: Sequential processing follows an arrangement of records; it differs from describing every retrieval as direct access.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: A communication protocol is best described as
options: Only the physical material of the cable.
Only the storage capacity of a server.
A database key that identifies one learner.
an agreed set of rules for exchanging data.
objectives.explanation: Protocols define aspects of communication such as message formats and exchange behaviour.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: A computer’s cooling vents are blocked by dust. What is a plausible consequence?
options: No electronic device can be affected by temperature.
Blocked vents convert RAM into permanent storage.
Restricted airflow can contribute to overheating and unreliable operation.
Dust automatically increases all processor performance.
objectives.explanation: Cooling depends on suitable airflow; cleaning and servicing should follow safe, competent procedures.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: Which arrangement is most consistent with a suitable computer workstation?
options: A requirement to twist continuously to see the screen.
A stable seat and screen position that support comfortable posture and clear viewing.
Cables across a walkway and a screen impossible to view comfortably.
A chair that cannot support the user at all.
objectives.explanation: Ergonomics concerns the user’s working arrangement rather than simply maximising screen brightness.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: In a conventional flowchart, which shape normally represents a decision with alternative paths?
options: Diamond.
Rectangle used for a processing step.
Arrow used only as a flow line.
Parallelogram used for input/output.
objectives.explanation: The decision symbol branches according to a condition; a rectangle commonly represents processing.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: A program outputs “Pass” if score≥50; otherwise it outputs “Retry”. What is output for score=50?
options: Retry
Both outputs at once under the stated rule.
No output because equality is undefined.
Pass
objectives.explanation: The ≥ comparison includes the boundary value 50.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: A score of 65 is accidentally entered as 56. Both satisfy the permitted range 0–100. Why might a range check fail to detect the error?
options: Range checks can detect every transposition automatically.
Verification is impossible if a number is valid.
Validation of permitted values is not the same as checking the value against the original source.
All values inside the range are guaranteed to be the intended values.
objectives.explanation: A plausible but incorrectly copied value can pass a range check; verification is still needed.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: A school needs the same letter layout with a different learner’s name on each copy. Which word-processing feature is most directly suitable?
options: Page orientation alone.
Mail merge using a template and a data source.
A spelling checker alone.
Manual independent copies with no shared template or data fields.
objectives.explanation: Mail merge combines standard text with variable fields; the question concerns document preparation, not automatically sending messages.

objectives.subject: Computer Studies
objectives.prompt: A photograph is publicly viewable online. What is the most responsible assumption before reusing it in a publication?
options: Public access does not itself establish permission; check the licence or obtain suitable permission.
Every publicly viewable image is automatically free of all restrictions.
Changing the filename always transfers ownership.
Removing the creator’s name always makes reuse lawful.
objectives.explanation: Visibility and reuse rights differ. The task does not assume a particular jurisdiction’s detailed exceptions.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: A historian compares a palace chronicle with a trader’s diary describing the same dispute. What is the main benefit?
options: The accounts can be checked against one another.
The older account automatically becomes false.
Both accounts become eyewitness records merely through comparison.
Differences between the accounts must be deleted.
objectives.explanation: Corroboration can reveal agreement, omissions and different perspectives; it does not guarantee truth.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Which evidence most directly helps date a buried settlement’s occupation when suitable organic material survives in a secure layer?
options: The present market price of a pot.
Radiocarbon dating of associated charcoal.
The modern spelling of a nearby town.
The colour preferred by a museum visitor.
objectives.explanation: Radiocarbon analysis estimates the age of organic remains; a secure archaeological context is essential.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: An oral tradition names several rulers but gives no calendar years. Which use is most defensible?
options: Assign exactly twenty years to every reign.
Discard it because all oral evidence is fictional.
Use its sequence alongside independently dated evidence.
Treat every generation as having identical length.
objectives.explanation: Oral accounts can preserve sequence and memory, but precise dating requires corroboration.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Nok culture is especially associated with which surviving material evidence?
options: Carved ivory court tusks.
Naturalistic brass portrait heads.
Cast copper-alloy ritual vessels.
Terracotta sculptures.
objectives.explanation: Terracotta figures are a characteristic surviving expression of Nok material culture.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: The elaborate copper-alloy objects from Igbo-Ukwu provide particularly strong evidence of
options: specialised metalworking skills.
the absence of local craftsmanship.
universal literacy in all nearby settlements.
industrial mass production using electric machines.
objectives.explanation: Complex cast objects demonstrate skilled production; they do not alone prove universal literacy or modern industry.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Which institution is most closely associated with the political leadership of precolonial Benin?
options: The Alaafin and the Oyo Mesi.
The Oba and the royal court.
The Shehu and the Bornu court.
The caliph and the emirate hierarchy.
objectives.explanation: The Oba was central to Benin kingship and its court institutions.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Why should an excavated bead resembling a foreign example not, by itself, prove that foreigners founded the settlement?
options: All beads are naturally formed stones.
Imported objects cannot be found in African settlements.
Trade can move objects without founding a settlement.
Trade always requires permanent conquest.
objectives.explanation: Objects can circulate through exchange; stronger evidence is needed to infer settlement origins.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Camel transport was important to trans-Saharan commerce principally because camels
options: eliminated the need for any route knowledge.
required rivers throughout the journey.
made every journey free from political risk.
could travel long desert routes with relatively little water.
objectives.explanation: Camel adaptation helped caravan travel across arid environments, though logistical and security challenges remained.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Which pair best illustrates complementary products exchanged across the Sahara historically?
options: West African gold and Saharan salt.
Saharan gold and West African rock salt as the dominant reverse flow.
Palm oil and Lancashire textiles as the defining medieval caravan exchange.
Gold Coast cocoa and European machine tools in early Saharan caravans.
objectives.explanation: Gold and salt were important, though not exclusive, commodities in trans-Saharan networks.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: How could long-distance trade encourage the spread of Islam in West Africa?
options: Commerce automatically converted every person by force.
Merchants and scholars carried religious ideas along trade networks.
Islam could spread only where no towns existed.
Caravan routes prevented contact between different communities.
objectives.explanation: Repeated contact through merchants and scholars facilitated transmission without implying uniform conversion.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: The nineteenth-century expression “legitimate commerce” in British West African policy generally referred to
options: a declaration that all earlier African trade had been illegal.
the end of all European commercial interests.
trade in commodities such as palm oil rather than enslaved people.
exclusive trade in human captives.
objectives.explanation: The historical term contrasted commodity trade with the slave trade; it did not imply that commodity production was always free of coercion.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Which conclusion about Atlantic slave trading is best supported by the forced removal of many working-age people?
options: It benefited every community equally.
It left population patterns entirely unchanged.
It prevented warfare in every affected region.
It could disrupt households and local production.
objectives.explanation: Forced displacement could alter labour, family structures and security, with effects differing across regions.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Why did the ending of British participation in the slave trade not immediately end slavery in West Africa?
options: A ban on a trade and the abolition of a labour status were different processes.
The terms slave trade and slavery always meant exactly the same law.
All West African societies were governed by one British parliament already.
No enslaved people remained anywhere after the ban.
objectives.explanation: Trade suppression, emancipation and enforcement occurred through different policies and timelines.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Usman dan Fodio is most closely associated with which nineteenth-century development?
options: The establishment of the Sefawa dynasty in Kanem.
The jihad that led to the Sokoto Caliphate.
The founding of Oyo under the Alaafin.
The emergence of Benin kingship under the Oba.
objectives.explanation: The jihad associated with Usman dan Fodio began in 1804 and led to the Sokoto Caliphate.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: The nineteenth-century Yoruba wars should be understood partly in relation to
options: a single unchanged empire controlling all Yoruba towns throughout the century.
the absence of competition over trade and security.
political fragmentation following the decline of Oyo.
the Nigerian Civil War of 1967–1970.
objectives.explanation: Oyo’s decline contributed to shifts in power, migration and competition among successor centres.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: A colonial railway links an inland produce district mainly to a seaport. Which economic purpose does this pattern most directly suggest?
options: Equal access to every village by design.
Ending all overseas trade.
Replacing the need for coastal ports.
Moving export produce towards overseas shipping.
objectives.explanation: Such alignment often prioritised export flows; a route map alone does not establish equal regional benefits.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: What makes a colonial official’s report on a protest a source requiring critical reading?
options: Its author may frame events to justify official actions.
Official documents can never contain accurate information.
Written reports have no identifiable authors.
Only spoken sources can contain a viewpoint.
objectives.explanation: Institutional interests can shape description; criticism weighs provenance and corroboration rather than rejecting all official evidence.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: The 1929 Women’s War in southeastern Nigeria is especially significant as evidence of
options: The rejection of British rule by a newly founded Sokoto cavalry state.
organised women’s resistance to colonial administration.
A dispute confined to elected male members of a national legislature.
A movement to restore Portuguese administration at the Niger Delta coast.
objectives.explanation: Women mobilised against colonial practices and perceived threats, including fears associated with taxation and enumeration.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Mission schools contributed to colonial-era social change partly by
options: ensuring identical access for every child immediately.
abolishing all indigenous systems of knowledge.
expanding Western-style literacy and training for some occupations.
ending regional inequalities automatically.
objectives.explanation: Schools created new opportunities but access was uneven and indigenous learning persisted.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Why did commodity export dependence expose colonial producers to overseas economic shocks?
options: Farm earnings were unrelated to sales.
Export prices were fixed permanently by local rainfall.
Overseas recessions always increased every commodity price.
Foreign demand and prices affected earnings.
objectives.explanation: Dependence on external markets transmitted changes in demand and prices to producers.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Which sequence is chronologically correct?
options: Amalgamation in 1914, independence in 1960, republic in 1963.
Independence in 1960, amalgamation in 1914, republic in 1963.
Republic in 1963, independence in 1960, amalgamation in 1914.
Amalgamation in 1914, republic in 1963, independence in 1960.
objectives.explanation: The three constitutional milestones occurred in 1914, 1960 and 1963 respectively.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: The Nigerian Civil War is conventionally dated
objectives.explanation: The war began in 1967 and ended in 1970; the other ranges refer to different periods.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: A study of post-war reconciliation would most directly examine
options: the terms of the 1886 treaty ending the Kiriji conflict.
the administration of territories before the 1914 amalgamation.
policies for reintegration and the experiences of affected communities.
the organisation of trade along precolonial caravan routes.
objectives.explanation: Reconciliation concerns relationships and reintegration after conflict, including how policies were experienced.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Two textbooks repeat the same unusual error from one older book. How should their agreement be treated?
options: As three independent eyewitness testimonies.
As proof that the error is correct.
As evidence that original sources are unnecessary.
As possibly dependent repetition rather than independent confirmation.
objectives.explanation: Sources derived from one another do not provide independent corroboration.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Which evidence would best test a claim that an oil boom benefited all Nigerian households equally?
options: Household and regional welfare evidence alongside national revenue data.
National export totals alone.
One oil-company advertisement alone.
A list of petroleum chemical properties alone.
objectives.explanation: Aggregate revenue cannot establish equal distribution; disaggregated evidence is needed.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: A coin is found in soil disturbed by recent building work. Why is dating the entire site from that coin risky?
options: Coins never carry historical information.
The coin may have been moved from its original layer.
All disturbed soil is older than undisturbed soil.
A single object always dates every feature nearby.
objectives.explanation: Disturbance weakens the association between an object and the layer in which it is found.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: A praise poem about a ruler is especially useful for investigating
options: a verbatim transcript of private discussions among the ruler’s enemies.
a precise independent calendar for every military campaign mentioned.
how supporters represented kingship and authority.
an unchanging account unaffected by performance or audience.
objectives.explanation: Praise poetry reveals political ideals and representation, while requiring care about selective celebration.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Which question most directly investigates the provenance of a historical letter?
options: How convincing is the writer’s argument?
Which later historian quoted it most often?
How far do its claims agree with excavated evidence?
Who wrote it, when, and for whom?
objectives.explanation: Provenance concerns a source’s origin and context, including authorship, date and audience.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Benin brass relief plaques are particularly valuable historical evidence for
options: representations of court life and hierarchy.
a complete chronological register of each ruler’s daily activities.
a representative census of households throughout the kingdom.
the private opinions of people who never appeared at court.
objectives.explanation: Court imagery preserves selected representations of rank and activity, not an exhaustive social record.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Which activity best demonstrates economic interdependence between a farming village and a craft town?
options: Each settlement obtaining everything without exchange.
Exchanging grain for tools made by specialist smiths.
A complete prohibition of all markets.
All inhabitants practising exactly the same occupation.
objectives.explanation: Specialisation creates complementary needs that exchange can satisfy.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: What most directly distinguishes trans-Saharan trade from transatlantic trade?
options: One necessarily used money while the other was entirely barter.
One linked only African traders while the other involved only Europeans.
Its principal routes crossed the Sahara rather than the Atlantic Ocean.
One carried only salt while the other carried only enslaved people.
objectives.explanation: The geographical routes differ; both networks changed over time and involved varied goods and people.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: The term Middle Passage refers specifically to
options: The outward European voyage carrying manufactured goods to Africa.
The return Atlantic voyage carrying American produce to Europe.
The inland movement of goods from a Saharan oasis to a West African market.
the forced Atlantic voyage of enslaved Africans to the Americas.
objectives.explanation: The term identifies the ocean crossing within Atlantic slave-trading networks.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: European industrial expansion encouraged nineteenth-century imperial competition partly through demand for
options: raw materials and markets.
the permanent abandonment of overseas commerce.
the elimination of shipping technology.
a universal ban on investment outside Europe.
objectives.explanation: Industrial interests were one factor among political and strategic motives for expansion.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Why is the Berlin Conference not evidence that African rulers freely consented to European partition?
options: Every African population voted in a common referendum there.
African rulers were not represented as equal negotiating participants.
The meeting was held before any European overseas contact.
Its purpose was to abolish all European territorial claims.
objectives.explanation: European powers negotiated rules for their rival claims without equivalent African participation.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Which event directly affected the royal court and cultural objects of Benin in 1897?
options: The annexation of Lagos as a British colony.
The creation of the Northern and Southern Nigeria protectorates.
A British military attack followed by extensive looting.
The amalgamation of the Northern and Southern administrations.
objectives.explanation: British forces attacked Benin City in 1897 and removed many royal objects.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: A merchant’s ledger lists growing palm-oil purchases. What additional evidence is needed before claiming local living standards rose?
options: Only a second copy of the same total.
The merchant’s signature enlarged.
A map showing Europe without local information.
Evidence of producer incomes, prices and access to resources.
objectives.explanation: Trade volume alone does not show who gained or how household welfare changed.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Which evidence best reveals African agency under colonial rule?
options: Records of negotiation, adaptation, petitions and resistance.
Assuming every policy was accepted without response.
Treating Africans only as unnamed recipients of policy.
Reading colonial orders as proof of automatic compliance.
objectives.explanation: Agency includes varied choices and responses, not only armed resistance.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Nigeria’s independence in 1960 and republican status in 1963 should be treated as
options: two dates for the same independence ceremony.
distinct constitutional milestones.
changes that both restored direct British colonial government.
measures that removed all regional government immediately.
objectives.explanation: Independence ended British colonial rule; republican status changed the constitutional head-of-state arrangement.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: Why should a history of urban growth examine migration as well as natural population increase?
options: Natural increase already includes every person moving into a town.
Migration affects employment but cannot affect population totals.
People moving into towns can change their size and composition.
Town populations are determined solely by births within their boundaries.
objectives.explanation: Migration is a separate component of urban change and may reshape occupations and social life.

objectives.subject: History
objectives.prompt: An exhibition labels an undated object “definitely made in 1500” solely because it looks old. What is the strongest criticism?
options: Every old-looking object is a modern forgery.
Objects cannot be studied historically.
An attractive label is sufficient proof.
A precise date requires evidence beyond appearance alone.
objectives.explanation: Stylistic impressions may inform a hypothesis but cannot alone justify a precise date.

objectives.subject: French
objectives.prompt: Complétez : « Après le repas, nous ___ au marché. » Choisissez le futur simple.
options: allons
allions
irons
sommes allés
objectives.explanation: Irons is the first-person plural future of aller; the other forms express different tenses.

objectives.subject: French
objectives.prompt: Choisissez la phrase correcte pour deux filles : « Hier, Amina et Binta ___ à huit heures. »
options: ont arrivées
sont arrivé
a arrivé
sont arrivées
objectives.explanation: Arriver takes être in the passé composé, and the participle agrees with the feminine plural subject.

objectives.subject: French
objectives.prompt: Complétez : « Il faut que vous ___ attentifs pendant la leçon. »
options: soyez
êtes
serez
étiez
objectives.explanation: Il faut que requires the subjunctive; soyez is the vous form of être.

objectives.subject: French
objectives.prompt: Quel mot remplace « à sa sœur » dans « Il écrit à sa sœur » ?
options: la
lui
le
elle
objectives.explanation: Écrire à quelqu’un takes an indirect-object pronoun: il lui écrit.

objectives.subject: French
objectives.prompt: Complétez : « Les lettres que Mariam a ___ sont sur la table. »
options: écrit
écrits
écrites
écrite
objectives.explanation: With avoir, a preceding direct object triggers agreement; lettres is feminine plural.

objectives.subject: French
objectives.prompt: Choisissez la réponse correcte : « Tu as des oranges ? — Oui, ___. »
options: je les suis
j’y suis
j’en suis
j’en ai
objectives.explanation: En replaces an indefinite quantity introduced by des with avoir.

objectives.subject: French
objectives.prompt: Complétez : « C’est le professeur ___ explique la règle. »
options: qui
que
dont
où
objectives.explanation: The relative pronoun is the subject of explique, so qui is required.

objectives.subject: French
objectives.prompt: Quelle phrase indique une action qui continue depuis deux ans ?
options: J’ai habité à Kano pendant deux ans, puis je suis parti.
J’habite à Kano depuis deux ans.
J’habiterai à Kano dans deux ans.
J’ai quitté Kano il y a deux ans.
objectives.explanation: Present tense with depuis describes a situation that began earlier and continues now.

objectives.subject: French
objectives.prompt: Complétez la condition : « Si j’avais assez de temps, je ___ ce roman. »
options: lirai
lis
lirais
ai lu
objectives.explanation: Si plus imperfect is normally followed here by the present conditional: je lirais.

objectives.subject: French
objectives.prompt: Choisissez le groupe nominal correct pour désigner une amie.
options: ma amie
mes amie
moi amie
mon amie
objectives.explanation: The possessive mon replaces ma before a feminine singular noun beginning with a vowel sound.

objectives.subject: French
objectives.prompt: Dans « Actuellement, la bibliothèque est fermée », actuellement signifie
options: en ce moment
en réalité, contrairement aux apparences
autrefois
demain seulement
objectives.explanation: Actuellement means currently; it is not equivalent to the English actually.

objectives.subject: French
objectives.prompt: Où va-t-on normalement pour acheter un roman neuf ?
options: À la bibliothèque pour l’emprunter.
À la librairie.
À la gare pour prendre le train.
À la pharmacie pour un médicament.
objectives.explanation: A librairie sells books; a bibliothèque lends or makes books available for consultation.

objectives.subject: French
objectives.prompt: Quel énoncé est le plus approprié pour demander poliment de répéter à une personne inconnue ?
options: Répète tout de suite !
Tu dois te taire !
Pourriez-vous répéter, s’il vous plaît ?
Je refuse de vous écouter.
objectives.explanation: The conditional and vous provide a polite request suitable for an unfamiliar adult.

objectives.subject: French
objectives.prompt: « Nous attendons le bus » veut dire que nous
options: écoutons une conférence dans le bus.
fabriquons un autobus.
avons déjà terminé le trajet.
restons jusqu’à son arrivée.
objectives.explanation: Attendre means to wait for, not to attend an event.

objectives.subject: French
objectives.prompt: Complétez : « Ce gâteau est bon, mais celui de ma tante est encore ___. »
options: meilleur
mieux
bien
le mieux
objectives.explanation: Meilleur compares the adjective bon describing gâteau; mieux compares the adverb bien.

objectives.subject: French
objectives.prompt: Pourquoi les livres étaient-ils difficiles à utiliser au début ?
options: Ils étaient tous écrits dans une langue inconnue.
Ils étaient enfermés dans des cartons sans classement.
Les habitants avaient interdit la lecture.
La salle était réservée aux jardiniers.
objectives.explanation: The opening describes cartons and the absence of a classification system.
objectives.passage: Chaque mercredi, après les cours, un groupe d’élèves ouvre une petite bibliothèque dans une salle prêtée par le quartier. Au début, les livres restaient enfermés dans deux cartons, car personne ne savait comment les classer. Une enseignante a proposé de les ranger par thèmes et de préparer des fiches de prêt. Depuis, les lecteurs retrouvent plus facilement les ouvrages. Pourtant, le groupe ne veut pas acheter beaucoup de nouveaux livres tout de suite. Il préfère d’abord demander aux habitants quels sujets les intéressent. Certains adultes cherchent des informations sur le jardinage, tandis que les plus jeunes souhaitent des histoires illustrées. Samedi prochain, les élèves organiseront une rencontre pour recueillir ces avis. L’entrée sera gratuite et chacun pourra proposer un titre. Les organisateurs espèrent ainsi choisir des achats utiles, au lieu de remplir les étagères de livres qui ne seraient jamais ouverts.

objectives.subject: French
objectives.prompt: Quel changement a facilité la recherche des ouvrages ?
options: La suppression des fiches de prêt.
La vente de tous les livres.
Le rangement par thèmes.
La fermeture de la salle.
objectives.explanation: The teacher’s thematic arrangement made books easier to find.

options: Pour interdire l’accès aux adultes.
Pour remplacer les livres par des cartons.
Pour faire payer la rencontre.
Pour connaître d’abord les intérêts des habitants.
objectives.explanation: Consulting residents is the stated reason for delaying purchases.

options: Aux souhaits des habitants concernant les lectures.
Aux horaires des trains.
Aux prix des cartons.
Aux notes scolaires de l’enseignante.
objectives.explanation: The demonstrative refers back to residents’ reading preferences.

options: Une bibliothèque réservée à la vente de plantes.
Une bibliothèque qui écoute ses lecteurs.
La disparition des livres illustrés.
Une rencontre obligatoire et payante.
objectives.explanation: The text centres on making useful choices through consultation.

objectives.subject: French
objectives.prompt: Qu’est-ce qui a entraîné le changement d’organisation des frères ?
options: La fermeture définitive du collège.
La disparition de tous les taxis.
Le nouvel horaire de travail de leur père.
Le déménagement du collège à l’étranger.
objectives.explanation: The father’s changed work schedule is explicitly the trigger.
objectives.passage: Pour aller au collège, Femi prenait autrefois un taxi avec son frère. Depuis que leur père a changé d’horaires de travail, ils doivent partir plus tôt. Femi a proposé de marcher jusqu’à l’arrêt principal et de prendre le bus. Son frère craignait surtout de manquer le premier cours. Ils ont donc essayé le nouveau trajet pendant une semaine, en notant chaque jour les heures de départ et d’arrivée. Le bus était moins cher, mais il arrivait parfois en retard lorsque la circulation était difficile. Les deux frères ont finalement décidé de garder cette solution les jours ordinaires et de prévoir un autre moyen de transport le jour d’un examen. Leur décision ne signifie pas que le bus est toujours lent. Elle montre simplement qu’ils distinguent le coût habituel du trajet et le risque particulier d’un retard important. Femi conserve encore ses notes pour vérifier si la situation s’améliore.

objectives.prompt: Quelle était la principale inquiétude du frère de Femi ?

Oublier un livre à la bibliothèque du quartier.
Marcher dans la salle de classe.
Arriver après le début du premier cours.
objectives.explanation: He feared missing the first lesson.

refuser toute observation.
